Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth exalts Allah, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.﴾ [al-Hadid 1]. The meaning of ﴿exalts﴾ (sabbaha) is: He declares Allah, Mighty and Majestic, free of every defect and deficiency, and free of resemblance to created beings. The proof that He is free of every defect and deficiency is the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿And We created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and no fatigue touched Us.﴾ [Qaf 38]. (Lughub) means: weariness and exhaustion, and this indicates the perfection of His power, Mighty and Majestic. And Allah, Exalted, says: ﴿Or do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private talk? Yes, and Our messengers are with them, recording.﴾ [az-Zukhruf 80]. And He, Exalted, says: ﴿And Allah is not unaware of what you do.﴾ [al-Baqarah 74], so He declared Himself free of heedlessness. And He, Exalted, says: ﴿And Allah is not to be frustrated by anything in the heavens or on the earth; indeed He is ever All-Knowing, All-Powerful.﴾ [Fatir 44], so He declared Himself free of incapacity.

In sum, tasbih means declaring Allah free of every deficiency and defect, and free of resemblance to created beings. The proof of this is His saying, Exalted: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.﴾ [ash-Shura 11].

Allah affirmed for Himself a face in His saying, Exalted: ﴿And there remains the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honour.﴾ [ar-Rahman 27]. Is the Face of Allah like the face of a created being?

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: What made you know that? Could it not be like the face of a created being? What is your evidence for that? Where is the evidence from the Qur'an or the Sunnah?

His saying, Exalted: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.﴾ [ash-Shura 11].

He affirmed for Himself that He istawa (rose/established Himself) over the Throne. A person istawa (sits firmly and rises) upon a camel, meaning he mounts the camel, settles on it and rises above it. Is Allah's istiwa' over the Throne like a person's istiwa' upon a camel? Impossible. What is the evidence? ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.﴾ [ash-Shura 11].

So every attribute that Allah affirms for Himself and that is also affirmed for a created being, its agreement is in name only; in reality, ﴿there is nothing like unto Him.﴾ Allah affirmed knowledge for Himself and affirmed knowledge for the created being. Allah said: ﴿If you know them to be believing women﴾ [al-Mumtahanah 10], so He affirmed knowledge for us, and He affirmed knowledge for Himself: ﴿Allah knows that you were deceiving yourselves﴾ [al-Baqarah 187]. Is the knowledge He affirmed for Himself like the knowledge of the created being?

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: The evidence?

* The student: (...).

* The Shaykh: May Allah bless you. So: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth exalts Allah﴾, sabbaha means declared free (of deficiency). Tanzih (declaring free) concerns two things: freedom from deficiency, and second, freedom from resemblance to created beings. Nothing among created things can resemble Him, neither in His essence nor in His attributes. For this reason we cannot comprehend Allah, Mighty and Majestic; we know Him through His signs, attributes and actions, but we do not grasp His reality, Mighty and Majestic, because however much you imagine, Allah, Exalted, is different from it and not like it.

His saying: ﴿whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾ means: everything in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and declares Him free (of imperfection). This includes the children of Adam, the jinn, the angels, insects, animals, everything. Everything in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah.

Does it glorify Him by the tongue of speech, meaning saying "Subhan Allah," or by the tongue of state, meaning that the arrangement of the heavens and the earth and the creatures as they are indicates the perfection of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and His freedom from every deficiency?

The answer: it glorifies Allah both by the tongue of state and by the tongue of speech, except the disbeliever, who glorifies Allah by the tongue of state but not by the tongue of speech, because the disbeliever ascribes to Allah every deficiency. He says: Allah has taken a son, and he says: there is another god with Him, and perhaps he denies the Creator altogether. But his state, his creation and his conduct are a glorification of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

So if we ask: is the glorification of what is in the heavens and the earth by the tongue of state or by the tongue of speech?

* A student: By the tongue of state and by the tongue of speech.

* The Shaykh: Except?

* The student: Except the disbeliever, who glorifies by the tongue of state but not by the tongue of speech.

* The Shaykh: Except the disbeliever, who glorifies by the tongue of state but not by the tongue of speech.

Do insects and animals glorify Allah by the tongue of speech? The answer: yes.

Allah, Exalted, says: ﴿And there is nothing but that it exalts Him with His praise, but you do not understand their glorification.﴾ [al-Isra' 44]. The ant glorifies Allah by the tongue of speech; all insects glorify Allah by the tongue of speech; the pebbles glorified Allah, as that happened in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) [narrated by al-Bazzar in his Musnad (4040) from the hadith of Abu Dharr]. But the disbeliever does not glorify Allah by the tongue of speech; rather, the opposite.

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth exalts Allah, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.﴾ ﴿Al-'Aziz﴾ means: possessor of might, and 'izzah is: greatness, dominance, authority and the like.

So al-'Aziz is the possessor of complete authority and complete dominance, so none can overpower Him, Mighty and Majestic. The pre-Islamic poet says:

Where is the escape, when the Seeking God is pursuing?
And al-Ashram, the vanquished one, is not the victor.

So: ﴿al-'Aziz﴾ means the one who prevails in His authority, power, might and otherwise.

﴿al-Hakim﴾ has two meanings. The first meaning: possessor of wisdom.

The second meaning: possessor of complete judgment.

It is derived from two things: from hikmah (wisdom) and hukm (judgment). Hikmah means that all His actions, sayings and legislation are wise, and there is no folly in them under any circumstances. For this reason, hikmah has been defined as: placing things in their fitting places. So there is no action of Allah or legislation of Allah except that it has a wisdom. If Allah decrees intense heat that destroys the fruits, that is wisdom without doubt; if Allah withholds rain, that is wisdom; if Allah sends death among people, that is wisdom; everything is wisdom. In legislation: when Allah makes trade lawful and forbids usury, that is wisdom in its permitting and wisdom in its forbidding, because we know that Allah is All-Wise; He distinguished between trade and usury: He made trade lawful and forbade usury.

If someone says: why? We say: Allah knows best; Allah is All-Wise. For this reason, when a woman said to 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her: "O Mother of the Believers, what about the menstruating woman making up the fast (i.e., if she menstruates during Ramadan) but not making up the prayer?" This is a question that presents a difficulty; one falls into a problem: why must a menstruating woman who breaks her fast in Ramadan make up the fast, but if she leaves the prayer she does not have to make up the prayer, when both are obligatory? She, may Allah be pleased with her, said: «We used to experience that, and we were commanded to make up the fast, and we were not commanded to make up the prayer» [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (321) and Muslim (335/69) from 'A'ishah].

She, may Allah be pleased with her, deduced the wisdom from the ruling, because we know that Allah is All-Wise, Mighty and Majestic; He did not obligate her to make up the fast rather than the prayer except for a wisdom. But sometimes we know the wisdom and sometimes we do not.

Usury and trade: why did Allah make trade lawful and forbid usury?

We say: because Allah made trade lawful and forbade usury. Therefore, when the people of usury said: "Trade is only like usury," Allah rejected their claim, saying: ﴿Allah has permitted trading and forbidden usury.﴾ [al-Baqarah 275].

So al-Hakim is derived from hikmah, which is placing a thing in its proper place. So when Allah judges something by legislation or judges something by decree, do not be perplexed. If Allah grants you success in knowing the wisdom, that is good; and if you do not know it, know that Allah is All-Wise.

Also, He has hukm (judgment), Mighty and Majestic. Allah, Exalted, says: ﴿Judgment belongs only to Allah; He has commanded that you worship none but Him.﴾ [Yusuf 40]. Judgment belongs to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Who can lift the judgment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when death comes upon someone?

* Students: No one.

* The Shaykh: No one. Allah, Exalted, says: ﴿Why, then, when it reaches the throat (83), and you are at that time looking on (84), and We are nearer to him than you, but you do not see (85), then why not, if you are not to be recompensed (86), return it (the soul), if you are truthful?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 83-87]. This cannot happen, because Allah has decreed it. If Allah, Mighty and Majestic, decrees wars and trials, who can lift them? Allah, Mighty and Majestic; judgment belongs to Him.

In legal matters, who judges between people by the Shari'ah? Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Allah, Exalted, says: ﴿And whatever you differ over, its judgment is with Allah﴾ [ash-Shura 10]. So judgment belongs to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. When you know that Allah, Exalted, possesses wisdom in what He legislates and what He creates and decrees, then you submit and do not dispute, because the One who judged thus is Allah. When you know that judgment belongs to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, among His servants, then to what do you refer in legal matters? To the Book and the Sunnah. In decreed matters you turn to Allah: if He decrees illness upon you, you seek refuge in Allah; if He decrees poverty upon you, you seek refuge in Allah: "O Allah, settle my debt for me and enrich me from poverty."

When a person believes that all judgment belongs to Allah, then if it is a decreed judgment he submits and says: this is the command of Allah, and I am a servant of Allah, and it cannot be other than what it is; and if it is a legislated judgment he says: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows best and judges what is good for the servants.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿He is the First and the Last, and the Manifest and the Hidden﴾ [al-Hadid 3]. These are four things.

﴿Al-Awwal﴾ (the First) means: there is nothing before Him. For if there were anything before Him, then Allah would be created, whereas He, the Mighty and Majestic, is the Creator. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ explained "the First" as the One before whom there is nothing; all existing things come after Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; there is no one with Allah and no one before Allah.

﴿Al-Akhir﴾ (the Last) is the One after whom there is nothing. For if there were anything after Him, then whatever came after Him would not be created by Allah; yet it is known that all creatures are created by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So He is the One after whom there is nothing.

So: He is the First without beginning, the Last without end, and nothing is after Him.

﴿Al-Zahir and al-Batin﴾ (the Manifest and the Hidden). As for al-Zahir, the Prophet ﷺ explained it when he said: "The One above whom there is nothing"[[Narrated by Muslim (2713/61) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]. All creatures are beneath Him, may He be exalted, so there is nothing above Him.

As for al-Batin (the Hidden), the Prophet ﷺ said: "The One beneath whom there is nothing"[[Narrated by Muslim (2713/61) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]. That is, nothing stands between Him and anything else. He is All-Aware, All-Knowing of everything; no mountains, trees, walls or anything else stands between Him and His creation. There is nothing beneath Him. The First and the Last encompass the generality of time, and the Manifest and the Hidden encompass the generality of place. We have said that these four names include comprehensiveness regarding time in His saying ﴿the First and the Last﴾, and regarding place in His saying ﴿the Manifest and the Hidden﴾.

﴿And He is Knowing of everything﴾ [al-Hadid 3]: Allah knows everything. ﴿Indeed, nothing on earth or in heaven is hidden from Allah﴾ [Al 'Imran 5]. If a person acts within his house, in a dark room, does Allah, exalted is He, know his deed? Yes.

He knows it. Moreover, He knows what your soul whispers, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And We have certainly created man, and We know what his soul whispers to him﴾ [Qaf 16]. When you think about something, Allah knows of it before it happens. Does He know the distant past? Yes. Everything. Does He know the distant future? Yes, everything. For this reason Musa, peace be upon him, when Fir'awn asked him: ﴿What then is the case of the former generations?﴾ [Ta-Ha 51], meaning: what is their condition? Tell us their story. He said: ﴿Its knowledge is with my Lord in a Book; my Lord neither errs nor forgets﴾ [Ta-Ha 52]. ﴿Neither errs﴾ means He does not lack knowledge, because ḍalāl (error) means ignorance, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said about His Prophet: ﴿And He found you ḍāll (lost) and guided you﴾ [al-Duha 7]. ﴿Ḍāll﴾ does not mean that he was a sinner; no, it means that he was ignorant and did not know, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor what faith was﴾ [al-Shura 52]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And you did not recite before it any scripture, nor did you write it with your right hand; otherwise the falsifiers would have had doubt﴾ [al-'Ankabut 48]. Therefore Allah is Knowing of everything.

O brother, if you know that Allah is Knowing of everything, can you commit an act of disobedience to Allah while you are hidden from people? Answer, answer, O group. Yes or no?

* Students: No.

* The Shaykh: No, because you know that Allah sees you; it is not possible. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Or do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private conversations? Yes, and Our messengers are with them, writing﴾ [al-Zukhruf 80]. So if you believe that Allah, exalted is He, is Knowing of everything, this necessarily entails that you do not disobey Him even in secret, and that you do not abandon His obedience even in secret. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, also said about Nuh, peace be upon him, that he said: ﴿And indeed, whenever I called them that You might forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears﴾ so as not to hear ﴿and covered themselves with their garments﴾ [Nuh 7], wrapping themselves so as not to see, may Allah protect us; because they hate the truth.

﴿And He is Knowing of all things﴾. Then: ﴿It is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days; then He established Himself above the Throne (al-'Arsh). He knows what enters into the earth and what comes out of it, and what descends from the heaven and what ascends into it﴾ [al-Hadid 4].

﴿Created the heavens and the earth﴾: He, Mighty and Majestic, brought them into being with complete order and measure. The heavens are seven, and the earths are seven. The earth preceded the heaven, because Allah, the Exalted, said in Surat Fussilat, when He mentioned the creation of the earth: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth: "Come willingly or unwillingly." They said: "We come willingly"﴾ [Fussilat 11]. He created the heavens and the earth, and the earth was created before the heavens. But Allah begins with the heavens because they are more noble than the earth and higher than the earth.

What about the heavens? Are they wrapped together in one layer, or is there a distance between them? There is a distance between them, and the distance is very, very great. This necessarily means that the smallest of the heavens is the lowest heaven, followed by the second, the third, and so on, each one wider than the one before it. They are of great size, and they are tiers (tibaq), matching one another, one above another. In the hadith of the Mi'raj (the Night Journey and Ascension), the Messenger (ﷺ), whenever he ascended to a heaven, asked for it to be opened, and it was opened for him. [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3887) and Muslim (164 / 264) from the hadith of Malik ibn Sasa'ah.]

﴿And the earth﴾: Allah, in the Qur'an, mentioned the earth in the singular form. The plural of "ard" is "aradun" (earths), and you will not find "aradun" in the Qur'an. Everywhere it is "ard." However, Allah indicated that there are multiple earths in His saying: ﴿Allah is He who created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them﴾ [al-Talaq 12]. That is, "the like of them" in number, not in attributes, because in attributes the resemblance between the earth and the heavens is very far off. But they are like them in number. The Sunnah has explicitly stated this in the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever seizes a span of land unjustly, Allah will collar him with it on the Day of Resurrection, from seven earths." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3198) and Muslim (1610 / 137) from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Zayd.]

He created them in six days. How many days? Allah, Mighty and Majestic, stated it without qualification. There is no indication whether a day is fifty thousand years or less or more. When it is stated without qualification, it is understood in its familiar, known sense, which is our days of today. It has come in a hadith that these days are Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday. Friday is the end of the creation of the heavens and the earth. Where did it begin? On Sunday. Saturday had no creation in it, neither a beginning nor an end. If someone says: "Is Allah not able to create them in an instant?"

The answer: Yes, indeed. His command, when He wills a thing, is to say to it "Be," and it is. So why were they created in six days? This is answered with two answers:

The first: these creatures follow one another in sequence, so Allah arranged some of them after others until He perfected them, and finished them in how many? Six days.

The second: Allah taught His servants deliberation and patience, and that what matters most is perfecting a thing, not finishing it. So a person may proceed deliberately in what he makes. Even if he could finish it in an hour, he may take his time, or finish it in two hours. Thus, Mighty and Glorified, He taught His servants patience in matters they are capable of. Both answers are sound.

﴿Then He established Himself above the Throne﴾: "Istawa 'alayhi" means "He rose above it" (ʿalā), in a manner befitting His majesty. We cannot liken it to the creation, because "there is nothing like unto Him" [al-Shura 11]. The Throne is a great creation whose measure is known only to the One who created it, Mighty and Majestic. It has come in a hadith: "The seven heavens and the seven earths, in comparison to the Footstool (al-Kursi), are like a ring thrown into a vast desert of the earth." What is the ring? The ring is a link of a coat of mail, the armor made of links of iron. What is a link of armor compared to a vast desert? What is its proportion? What space does it occupy of the earth? Nothing. "The seven heavens and the seven earths, in comparison to the Footstool, are nothing but like a ring thrown into a desert of the earth, and the superiority of the Throne over the Footstool is like the superiority of the desert over that ring." [Sahih Ibn Hibban (361) from the hadith of Abu Dharr.] La ilaha illa Allah! Therefore no one knows its measure except Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It is not for us to ask: "What is the material of this Footstool? From where is its material? Gold, silver, pearls?" We have no right to speak about this. It is a Throne, great, as Allah described it: ﴿Lord of the Great Throne﴾ [al-Tawbah 129], ﴿the Glorious Throne﴾ [al-Buruj 15]. It is a very, very great Throne, whose measure no one knows except Allah. Allah established Himself upon it in perfection of His dominion, may He be exalted.

You may find in some books: "istawa 'ala al-'arsh" means "istawla 'alayhi" (He seized control of it). Do you sometimes find this? Whoever among you has looked into some books of the Ash'arites (al-Ash'ariyyah, a theological school) and their like will see this: "istawa" is interpreted as "istawla." This is distortion of words from their proper places (tahrif), and speaking about Allah without right and without knowledge. Because if the creation of the heavens was followed by "then He established Himself upon the Throne," we would say "then He seized the Throne." Before the seizing, to whom did the Throne belong?! See the falsehood of this statement. Then we would say that Allah "istawa" (seized) everything. Would we say He "istawa" upon the earth? This cannot be said. So it is necessary that "istawa" means "'alā" (rose above). How He established Himself, we do not know; Allah knows best.

﴿He knows what enters into the earth and what comes out of it, and what descends from the heaven and what ascends into it﴾ [al-Hadid 4].

﴿What enters into the earth﴾: that is, what enters it of corpses, of seeds that sprout by the permission of Allah, of waters that Allah channels as springs in the earth, then brings forth, and other things, including insects and others. In short, everything that enters the earth, Allah knows it.

Now our question: Does He know the state of the ants when they enter their holes? Does He know or not?

* Students: He knows.

* The Shaykh: It is not mentioned in the verse, but we say: ﴿What enters﴾, here "ma" is a relative pronoun (ism mawsul), and the relative pronoun conveys generality, meaning: everything that enters the earth.

﴿And what comes out of it﴾: of plants, waters, minerals, and others.

﴿And what descends from the heaven﴾: of angels, rain, revelations (shara'i'), and other things.

﴿And what ascends into it﴾: that is, toward it. But ﴿fīhā﴾ ("into it") came instead of "ilayhā" ("toward it") so that we benefit from two benefits:

The first benefit: the ascent, meaning the rising.

The second benefit: entry, because the preposition "fi" (in) suits verbs of entering: he entered into a place. But "'araja" and "ya'ruju" are suited by "ila" (to). However, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, departed from saying "ya'ruju ilayhā" to saying ﴿ya'ruju fīhā﴾ to convey what? The ascent and the entry. Things do not reach the lowest heaven and stop there; they ascend within the heaven until they reach Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

So, ﴿ya'ruju fīhā﴾: if one of the grammarians asks you: "Why did 'fī' come instead of 'ilā,' when the Qur'an is eloquent?" What is the answer? We say: "ya'ruju" has implicitly included the meaning of "yadkhulu" (enters), and this implication (tadmin) exists in the Noble Qur'an and in the Arabic language. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿A spring from which the servants of Allah drink, making it gush forth in abundance﴾ [al-Insan 6]. What is appropriate with "yashrabu" (drinks)? "Min" (from), as He said: ﴿He eats of what you eat, and drinks of what you drink﴾ [al-Mu'minun 33], meaning "minhu" (from it). ﴿So they drank from it, except a few of them﴾ [al-Baqarah 249]. Here He said ﴿yashrabu bihā﴾ ("drink with it"). What is the wisdom? The scholars said: the wisdom is that "yashrabu" here implicitly includes the meaning of "yarwā bihā" (quench one's thirst with it), and it is known that when you say "yarwā bihā" it includes the meaning of "yashrabu" plus more. This implication is an important art in the field of eloquence (balaghah). The student of knowledge should study it and verify it, so that he benefits from it when the particles differ with their governing verbs, and it does not confuse him.

﴿And He is with you wherever you are, and Allah﴾: the pronoun "huwa" refers to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. ﴿Ma'akum﴾ ("with you") means: accompanying you, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, You are the Companion on the journey, and the Successor over the family." [Narrated by Muslim (1342 / 425) from the hadith of Ibn Umar.]

But is this companionship a companionship of place, in the sense that when we are in a place, Allah is with us? Far from it, absolutely not. This cannot be. How can a sensible person imagine that Allah is with us in our place, when His Footstool encompasses the heavens and the earth? This is impossible. The Footstool is the place of the feet, as came from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) [narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12404)]. If that is so, is it conceivable that the Lord of the heavens and the earth, on the Day of Resurrection, when the heavens are folded up in His right hand and the earth is His handful, could be with us in our narrow or wide places? It is not possible.

So ﴿ma'akum﴾ means: accompanying you. The one who accompanies may be far from you. The Arabs say in their speech: "We kept traveling and the moon was with us," "We kept traveling and the Pole Star was with us," "We kept traveling and such-and-such mountain was with us." Is the moon in their place? It is known that the moon is in the sky, and the star is in the sky, and the mountain may be days' distance from you, yet the Arabs describe it as "with" them despite distance in place. Our belief that Allah is with us means that He knows us, does He not? He hears our words, sees our deeds, has power over us and dominion, and manages our affairs in every sense that companionship requires.

Know that among the misguided are those who say: "Allah is with us in our places," may Allah protect us, while denying that Allah is above, exalted in the heaven. They have committed two great calamities: denying the highness of Allah, and the second, believing that He is in the earth.

Glory be to Allah! Is it conceivable that a sensible person, let alone a believer, would believe that if he is in the privy, in the toilet, Allah is with him?! I seek refuge in Allah! Whoever believes this, I testify before Allah that he is a disbeliever, because the greatest mockery of Allah and the greatest belittling of Allah's status is this.

Then we say: If Allah were, as they claim, everywhere, meaning that He is in the room, in the market, in the mosque, then who would be with some people in the room and other people in the street? Are they two gods? Answer, O people!

* Students: No.

* The Shaykh: No. It is impossible for them to say that Allah is multiple. If there are not two gods, is He divisible, part of Him here and part of Him there? Then it follows that His being with us in our places in His essence is void, because He would either be multiple or divisible, and both are false. I have established this because there now exist, as we have observed among those who come to Makkah, people who hold this belief.

Allah says: ﴿And He is with you﴾. This is a verse, ﴿And He is with you﴾. What does it say? We say: "ma'iyyah" (being with) is companionship, and companionship does not necessarily imply being co-located in place, meaning being settled in your place. This does not follow. How could Allah, Exalted, be with you in your place when He, Glorified and Exalted, encompasses in His Footstool the heavens and the earth? But those who believe this have not measured Allah with His true measure, nor magnified Him with true magnification, nor known His greatness and majesty. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿They did not measure Allah with His true measure, while the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand﴾ [al-Zumar 67]. So how can one believe that Allah is with us in our place?

Therefore a person must recognize the blessing of Allah upon him in that he believes in the Qur'an as it is, according to its apparent meaning, magnifying Allah with true magnification.

As for His saying ﴿wherever you are﴾: that is, in whatever place you are, because "ayna" is a adverb of place. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿So turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque; and wherever you are, turn your faces toward it﴾ [al-Baqarah 144], like ﴿wherever you are﴾.

﴿And Allah is All-Seeing of what you do﴾ [al-Hadid 4]: that is, of all the deeds you do, He is All-Seeing. Is the sight here sight of knowledge or sight of vision? It includes both. He is All-Seeing with the sight of vision; He sees us, Mighty and Majestic. The Prophet (ﷺ) said about his Lord: "His veil is light; if He were to unveil it, the splendors of His face would burn away whatever of His creation His sight reaches." [Narrated by Muslim (179 / 293) from the hadith of Abu Musa.] This is sight of vision.

As for the sight of knowledge: it is known that our deeds may be visible, like movements, and may be audible, like words. What is audible is not seen by the eye, but it is heard. Hearing what is heard is knowledge. On this basis we say: ﴿And Allah is All-Seeing of what you do﴾ [al-Hadid 4] includes both knowledge and sight by vision.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 57, verse 5:

﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Hadid: 5]. ﴿To Him﴾ means: to Allah alone, ﴿the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾, in both creation and management. No one owns the heavens and the earth except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, neither independently nor in partnership. Allah says: ﴿Say: Call upon those you claim besides Allah. They do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth, and they have no share in them, nor is there for Him from among them any supporter﴾ [Saba': 22]. Thus He negated independent ownership and negated partnership. ﴿Nor is there for Him from among them any supporter﴾ [Saba': 22], meaning: no helper who assisted Him in creating the heavens and the earth. So dominion over the heavens and the earth belongs to Him. How many heavens are there?

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Seven? No. The heavens are greater than the earth, so could their number be ten? I do not think anyone would still be ignorant of this. Their number is seven. Allah says: ﴿Say: Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Mighty Throne?﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 86]. The earths are also seven, as this is apparent in the Qur'an and explicit in the Sunnah. Allah says: ﴿Allah is the One who created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them﴾ [al-Talaq: 12], meaning in number. And it is established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever unjustly takes a span of land, Allah will collar him with it on the Day of Resurrection from seven earths."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3198) and Muslim (1610 / 137) from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Zayd.]]

﴿And to Allah all matters are returned﴾ [al-Hadid: 5]: all matters, meaning the affairs general and specific, religious and worldly, of the Hereafter and of this world, all of them return to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. He disposes as He wills and judges as He wills, and none can repel His judgment, the Mighty and Majestic. All matters. Are a person's personal matters returned to Allah?

Answer: Yes.

They return to Allah. Therefore, when a calamity befalls you, you must turn to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because when polytheists are struck by calamities they cannot bear, they turn to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. When winds batter them in the depths of the seas on their ships, to whom do they turn? To Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. They turn to Allah, asking Him to deliver them, while they are polytheists. So how about you, O Muslim! Turn to Allah in everything, small or great, religious or worldly, concerning yourself or your family. Do not turn to other than Allah. Whoever brings his need to Allah, it is fulfilled, and whoever brings his need to other than Allah is left to that other.

So we say: ﴿And to Allah all matters are returned﴾. Which matters? Say it, everyone.

* Students: All matters.

* The Shaykh: All matters, the matters in general: the religious, the worldly, and the Hereafter, the worldly and the personal and the general. And if you believe this, and you must believe it, you will not turn to anyone but Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 57, verse 6:

﴿He causes the night to enter into the day, and He causes the day to enter into the night﴾ [al-Hadid: 6] ﴿yuliju﴾: i.e., He makes the night enter into the day, and ﴿He causes the day to enter﴾ i.e., He makes it enter into the night. This means the night and day differ in length and shortness. Sometimes the night begins to increase, as in our times now; the night has now begun to increase. The night begins to increase, so does it enter upon the day, or does the day enter upon it?

* Students: It enters upon the day.

* The Shaykh: It enters upon the day. This is "He causes the night to enter into the day." Sometimes the night begins to decrease and the day increases, so which one enters? The day enters upon the night. No one is able to do this except Allah, the Exalted, even if all creation gathered together: their humans and their jinn, mankind and the angels. They would not be able to cause even one minute of the night to enter into the day, or of the day to enter into the night, while Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night.

Then, this entering does not come all at once. You cannot say: the shortest night becomes the longest night within two days. That is not possible. Rather, it comes gradually, little by little. At first, when the increase begins, you find it takes a little, perhaps one minute over two or three days, then it keeps increasing until, at the equality of night and day, it reaches about two minutes per day. It is gradual. Consider if it came all at once: suppose we were on the longest day of the year and, behold, the next day we were on the shortest day of the year. What would follow from that? Great corruptions, because people would move from a disturbing heat to a painful cold within twenty-four hours, and there is no doubt that this is harmful to bodies, plants and the climate. But He, the Mighty and Majestic, causes it to enter in an arrangement that is perfectly in accord with wisdom, and no one, by Allah, can ever do this, however great his strength.

﴿And He is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾ [al-Hadid: 6]. (Dhat al-Sudur) means the hearts. (Dhat al-Sudur) means the possessors of the breasts, i.e., the hearts. The evidence that it means the hearts is the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿For indeed, it is not the eyes that are blind, but blind are the hearts which are within the breasts﴾ [al-Hajj: 46]. So: He knows what is in the heart. Do you believe this? You believe it, because the report is from whom? It is the report of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And who is more truthful in statement than Allah?﴾ [an-Nisa: 122]. If you believe this, is it possible for you to harbour in your heart what Allah does not approve? If you are a believer, it is not possible. Purify your heart of showing off, hypocrisy, rancour towards the Muslims, spite and hatred. Purify it, because your heart is known to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. O Allah, purify our hearts; O Allah, purify our hearts; O Allah, purify our hearts. Purify the heart of this, and fill it with love of Allah and magnifying Him, and love of the Messenger (ﷺ) and magnifying him as is fitting for him, and love of the believers, and love of the Sharia of Allah, even if you dislike it. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said to the Companions: ﴿Fighting has been enjoined upon you while it is hateful to you. But perhaps you hate a thing and it is good for you; and perhaps you love a thing and it is bad for you. And Allah knows, while you know not﴾ [al-Baqarah: 216].

Do not harbour in this lump of flesh anything that Allah dislikes. If you do, Allah is Knowing of it, nothing is hidden from Him. So purify your heart until it is pure and sound, for on the Day of Resurrection no one benefits except one who comes to Allah with a sound heart, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿The Day when neither wealth nor children will benefit, except one who comes to Allah with a sound heart﴾ [ash-Shu'ara: 88-89].

The changes of the heart are rapid and wondrous. It may shift from disbelief to faith, or from faith to disbelief, in a moment. We ask Allah for steadfastness. The change of the heart follows what surrounds a person, and what most causes the heart to change towards corruption is love of this world. Love of this world is a calamity, and it is strange that we are attached to it while we know that it is the enjoyment of delusion, and that a person, if he is pleased one day, is displeased another day, as the poet said:

"One day is for us and one day against us, and one day we are made to suffer and one day we are made happy."

Every pleasure in this world is surrounded by something that spoils it. Therefore, be keen to purify the heart from attachment to this world, except in what benefits you in the Hereafter. For example, that you be attached to this world so that you become wealthy and spend your wealth in the way of Allah and in what pleases Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; that is something else. Seeking wealth for righteous deeds is good, but seeking wealth to compete with the people of this world in their worldly affairs is evil.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 57, verse 7:

﴿Believe in Allah and His Messenger, and spend from that of which He has made you successors.﴾ [al-Hadid: 7] ﴿Believe﴾: the address is to all of the servants. ﴿In Allah﴾, the Lord of the worlds, ﴿and His Messenger﴾, Muhammad (ﷺ). The command here is for obligation, which is the strongest type of obligation in its certainty. Belief in Allah means that you believe He is the Lord of the worlds; that you believe He is the true God who alone deserves worship; that you believe He has the most beautiful names and the highest attributes; that you believe He does what He wills; that you believe there is none to repel His judgment, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing; and that you believe the creation will return to Him in the legal rulings and in the universal decrees. So who manages creation? Who?

None manages creation except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; He manages His affair.

Who judges between them concerning that about which they differ? Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), whom Allah, exalted is He, sent to all creation, both humans and jinn, and with whom He sealed the prophethoods, so there is no prophet after him. The evidence is: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any of your men, but he is the Messenger of Allah and the seal of the prophets﴾ [al-Ahzab: 40], meaning and he was the Messenger of Allah and ﴿the seal of the prophets﴾ [al-Ahzab: 40], so there is no prophet after him. Whoever claims prophethood after him is a disbeliever, and it is obligatory that his neck be cut off unless he repents and returns.

He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Believe in Allah and His Messenger, and spend from that of which He has made you successors﴾ [al-Hadid: 7]. Infaq (spending, i.e., giving freely) means giving. ﴿From that of which He has made you successors﴾ means wealth, because Allah has made us successors in this wealth. It is He who made us its owners, so we have no favour upon Allah by what we spend; rather, the favour is Allah's upon us by what He has given, and His favour upon us by what He has legislated for us regarding spending. Had Allah not legislated for us to spend, spending would have been a waste and an innovation. But He legislated for us to spend. So, first, He has the favour for what He made us own of wealth, and second, He has the favour for what He legislated for us of spending from it.

﴿So those of you who believe and spend, for them is a great reward﴾ [al-Hadid: 7]. Those who believed in whom? In Allah and His Messenger, since He said: ﴿Believe in Allah and His Messenger, and spend﴾, i.e., from that in which He made them successors, for them is a great reward. As you know, the verses describe their reward as great and immense: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times its like﴾ [al-An'am: 160]. So the reward is abundant. Allah described the rewards for deeds with these attributes: great, immense, abundant. We take the "abundant" from His saying: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times its like﴾. Through this you know the favour of Allah, exalted is He, upon us, and praise be to Allah. He commands us to act, we act by it, and He rewards us for it with abundant reward, immense reward, great reward, a great and mighty favour. So it is upon us to thank Allah and to spend from that in which He has made us successors.

Should we spend all that we possess or part of it? In ﴿spend from that which He has made you﴾, is the "min" (from) here for partitive (tab'id) or for explanation (bayan), explaining what is to be spent from it? If it is partitive, the meaning is: spend part of what He has made you, which is all of it. If we take it as explanatory, the meaning is: spend from what He has made you according to what the benefit requires, either all or part. Which of them is better? That we make "min" partitive or make "min" explanatory? The second: if we make it explanatory, the person becomes free to spend all his wealth or part of his wealth, most or least, according to what benefit requires.

It is known that whenever the meaning is broader, it is more fitting to adopt it, and the Noble Qur'an has broad, great meanings. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) once urged charity, and the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, used to race to goodness, each one loving to be the foremost. So 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Today I will outdo Abu Bakr," because these two men were the closest of the Companions to the Messenger (ﷺ), and the most beloved of the Companions to the Messenger (ﷺ).

The Prophet (ﷺ) loves Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) more intensely than he loves 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), although 'Ali was his cousin and the husband of his daughter. But he loves Abu Bakr more intensely and more greatly. He was asked: "Who is the most beloved of people to you?" He said: "Abu Bakr." [Narrated by Abu Dawud (1678) and al-Tirmidhi (3675), from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.] This is his statement, and his statement is true; is there any doubt in it? It is true and there is no doubt about this. He (ﷺ) said: "If I were to take a close friend from my Ummah, I would have taken Abu Bakr." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (466) and Muslim (2382/2), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id.]

In sum, 'Umar and Abu Bakr were like two horses in a race; 'Umar wanted to outdo him, not out of envy of Abu Bakr, but out of love for virtue for himself. He said: "Today I will outdo Abu Bakr," so he came with half of his wealth to spend it. Half of his wealth, meaning if he had two hundred, two thousand, two million, half of his wealth. He brought it to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "O 'Umar, what have you left for your family?" He said: "I left them the half," meaning the half. Then Abu Bakr came, and he (ﷺ) said: "What have you left for your family?" He said: "I left them Allah and His Messenger." He gave all his wealth. 'Umar said: "By Allah, I will never race you in anything after this, ever." [Narrated by Ahmad in Fada'il al-Sahabah (527), from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.] He knew he was unable to outdo Abu Bakr.

What is the proof from this hadith? That Abu Bakr gave in charity all of his wealth. So if a person sees the benefit in giving away all of his wealth, and that he has the strength of trust in Allah, reliance upon Him, and earning provision, such that he can take back nothing of the wealth for his family and himself, then we say: give away all your wealth, spend all your wealth. But if the matter is the opposite, if he is a clumsy man who does not know how to earn, and there is no need for him to spend much, then here we say: it is better that you spend part of the wealth.

So, O brothers, in ﴿spend from that which He has made you﴾, is "min" partitive or explanatory? Explanatory, meaning: spend from this wealth that which contains benefit.

In this verse is evidence that a person should realize and establish his faith, and whenever he sees in it any wavering, he should seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan and continue on his path, and that he should spend from wealth.

Here is a question: is wealth beloved to souls?

Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And you love wealth with abundant love﴾ [al-Fajr: 20], and He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And indeed, he is intense in his love of good﴾, meaning wealth [al-'Adiyat: 8]. A person cannot give up something beloved to him except for what is more beloved. So when a person gives up what is beloved to him, seeking the good pleasure of Allah, we know that the man loves Allah's good pleasure more than his love for wealth, and by this faith is realized.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 57, verse 8:

﴿And what is [there] for you that you do not believe in Allah, while the Messenger invites you to believe in your Lord, and He has already taken your covenant, if you are [truly] believers?﴾ [al-Hadid: 8] This is coordinated with the verse before it, which is His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿Believe in Allah and His Messenger, and spend from that in which He has made you successors. So those among you who have believed and spent will have a great reward.﴾ (7) ﴿And what is [there] for you that you do not believe in Allah?﴾ [al-Hadid: 7-8] Meaning: What is it that prevents you from believing in Allah, when the causes that make belief in Him obligatory have been completed? This is through the call of the Prophet (ﷺ), as the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿while the Messenger invites you to believe in your Lord, and He has already taken your covenant﴾. Meaning, Allah has taken your covenant: the pledge that you would believe in Him and in His messengers. Thus there are two causes for belief:

The first: the call of the Prophet (ﷺ) to it.

The second: the covenant which Allah has taken from us, and this is by what the Mighty and Majestic has given us of natural disposition (fitrah), intellect and understanding, by which we perceive what benefits us and what harms us. This is the correct meaning of the covenant. It has also been said that it is the covenant which Allah, the Exalted, took from the children of Adam when He brought them forth from their loins, if the hadith narrated concerning that is authentic.

The essential point is that Allah, the Exalted, rebukes the one who does not believe and says: What has moved you not to believe, when the causes making belief obligatory have been completed through the call of the Messenger (ﷺ) and the taking of the covenant?!

﴿if you are [truly] believers﴾ Meaning: if you are believers, then hold fast to belief in Allah and His Messenger.

﴿He is the One who sends down to His servant clear signs﴾ [al-Hadid: 9]. When He mentioned that the Prophet ﷺ calls people to faith, He explained that he (ﷺ) brought clear signs, meaning indications that testify to his truthfulness and that what he brought is true. "Clear" means manifest, through what they contain of beneficial narratives, truthful reports, just rulings, complete eloquence, and wondrous expression. The Arabs, who were the masters and leaders of eloquence, were challenged by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, several times to produce the like of this Qur'an, and they were unable to do so. So He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿He is the One who sends down to His servant clear signs﴾, meaning signs that indicate he is truly the Messenger of Allah and that what he brought is true, because of what they contain of truthful reports, just rulings, beneficial narratives, eloquence and rhetorical excellence, and other things that are well known.

His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿that He may bring you out from the darknesses into the light﴾ [al-Hadid: 9]. The pronoun in ﴿that He may bring you out﴾ may refer to the Messenger ﷺ, meaning that he would be the means of bringing you out from darknesses into light. It may also refer to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, meaning that Allah, exalted is He, would bring you out from darknesses into light through these signs. Both meanings are true. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Allah is the Guardian of those who believe; He brings them out from the darknesses into the light﴾ [al-Baqarah: 257], and He says: ﴿A Book which We have sent down to you, that you may bring mankind out from the darknesses into the light﴾ [Ibrahim: 1]. So the Prophet ﷺ is the means by which people are brought out from darknesses into light, while the one who actually brings them out is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

By "darknesses" is meant the darknesses of ignorance, the darknesses of shirk (associating partners with Allah), the darknesses of transgression, and the darknesses of disobedience. Everything that opposes the truth is darkness, and everything that agrees with it is light.

So, His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿that He may bring you out﴾, to whom does the pronoun refer? The pronoun in "that He may bring you out" refers to whom?

* Student: The kaf (the "you").

* The Shaykh: The kaf refers to the people, but the subject, the pronoun, refers to whom? Either to Allah or to the Messenger.

What supports that it refers to Allah? The saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿Allah is the Guardian of those who believe; He brings them out from the darknesses into the light﴾ [al-Baqarah: 257]. And what supports that it refers to the Messenger? ﴿A Book which We have sent down to you, that you may bring mankind out from the darknesses into the light﴾ [Ibrahim: 1]. When a verse may carry two meanings that do not contradict each other, it is taken as having both of them. So Allah is the one who truly brings out, and the Messenger brings out as a means.

﴿And indeed, Allah is Kind and Merciful to you﴾ [al-Hadid: 9]. This sentence is a declarative one, emphasized with "inna" (indeed) and the lam. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Kind and Merciful to you﴾. Ra'fah (kindness, tenderness) is the most refined form of mercy, while rahmah (mercy) is more general. So He, the Mighty and Majestic, is Ra'uf and Rahim, meaning He is possessor of mercy toward the believers, the Mighty and Majestic, as He says: ﴿And He has always been Merciful to the believers﴾ [al-Ahzab: 43]. Allah's mercy, exalted is He, is either general or specific. The general mercy encompasses all people, and the specific mercy is for the believers, as He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And He has always been Merciful to the believers﴾ [al-Ahzab: 43].

If someone asks: what mercy does Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, show to the disbeliever?

The answer: He provides him with livestock, children, reason, security and sustenance. Indeed, their good things are hastened to them in their worldly life, is that not so? Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And if Allah were to take mankind to account for their wrongdoing, He would not leave upon it [the earth] any creature, but He defers them to a specified term﴾ [al-Nahl: 61].

So if someone asks you: Does Allah have mercy on the disbeliever? Do not say "yes" or "no" outright. In the general sense, yes, He has mercy on him, and were it not for Allah's mercy toward him, he would have perished. But in the specific sense, no. The specific mercy is for the believers only, as the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿And He has always been Merciful to the believers﴾ [al-Ahzab: 43].

﴿And indeed, Allah is Kind and Merciful to you (9). And what is [the matter] with you that you do not spend in the cause of Allah﴾ [al-Hadid: 10]. Listen, so that you know that the Qur'an connects with itself. Allah the Exalted said at the beginning of these verses: ﴿Believe in Allah and His Messenger, and spend from that of which He has made you successors﴾ [al-Hadid: 7]. Then He said: ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not believe in Allah﴾ [al-Hadid: 8]. Then He said: ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not spend in the cause of Allah﴾. When He commanded us to spend from that in which He made us successors, He said: ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not spend in the cause of Allah﴾. That is: what prevents you? Spending in the cause of Allah (infaq fi sabil Allah) includes everything that Allah has commanded to be spent on. So "in the cause of Allah" here is general, and therefore it includes spending on oneself, spending on one's wife, spending on one's family, spending on the poor and the orphans, and spending in the cause of Allah. Everything that Allah has commanded to be spent on is included in this verse. Even on oneself? Yes. Your spending on yourself is charity (sadaqah), your spending on your wife is charity. But pay attention to the intention (niyyah), because of the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) to Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas: "And know that you will not spend an expenditure by which you seek the Face of Allah except that you will be rewarded for it" [Agreed upon: al-Bukhari (56) and Muslim (1628/5) from the hadith of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas]. This condition is necessary, it is indispensable: that by it you seek the Face of Allah. "Except that you will be rewarded for it," meaning: it will be recorded for you.

So, ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not spend in the cause of Allah﴾: what is meant by spending in the cause of Allah? Everything that Allah has commanded to be spent on.

﴿And to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Hadid: 10]. That is: how can you not spend, when it is Allah who will inherit the heavens and the earth? And from among (...) your wealth which you were stingy with, Allah the Mighty and Majestic will inherit it. So when your wealth is inherited after you, either a righteous person inherits it, and then he will be happier with it than you, or a corrupt person inherits it, and you will have left behind for him what he uses to corrupt [others]. Have you understood this? If you leave wealth behind, either you leave it to someone who will spend it in the cause of Allah, and then he will be happier with your wealth than you, or you leave it to a corrupter who will use it to disobey Allah, and then you will have helped him to disobey Allah with the wealth you left for him.

So what is most fitting for you? That you spend it in the cause of Allah, so that it is a gain for you and you are safe from its harm, should it be inherited by one who corrupts with it.

Remember, my brother: when you think about spending, Satan comes to you, commands you to be stingy, and promises you poverty. Reflect that if you leave this wealth behind, it must be inherited. It will not be buried with you; it must be inherited. And the inheritance will revolve between the two matters I mentioned: either it is inherited by one who spends it in the cause of Allah, and then he will be happier with your wealth than you, or it is inherited by one who uses it to spread corruption on the earth, and then you will have been a cause of corruption on the earth. This is unavoidable.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth. Not equal among you are those who spent and fought before the conquest﴾ [al-Hadid: 10].

Spent in what? In the cause of Allah. "Not equal among you are those who spent in the cause of Allah and fought," meaning: compared with those who did not spend and did not fight. It is impossible that this and that be equal, because the religion of Islam is a religion of justice in deeds and recompense. Pay attention! A religion of justice in what? In deeds and recompense. It is not, as the modern innovators (al-muhdathun al-muhdithun) say, a religion of equality. This is a great error, but people of corrupt opinions and ideas use it to reach blameworthy aims, until one says: woman and man are equal, the believer and the transgressor are equal, the Arab and the non-Arab are equal, and there is no difference. Subhan Allah! You will not find in the Qur'an the word "equality" between people; there must be difference. Rather, most of the Qur'an is a negation of equality: ﴿not equal﴾.

﴿Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?﴾ [az-Zumar: 9], and many other verses.

So beware of following [this trend], so that you become like one who shouts at what hears nothing but supplication and calling. Instead of saying "the Islamic religion is a religion of equality," say: it is a religion of justice, which Allah commanded, that every rightful person be given his right. Do you see that a woman and a man are equal in inheritance, or do they differ? They differ. In blood money (diyah)? The blood money for a woman is half the blood money for a man. In the 'aqiqah (sacrifice for a newborn)? Ransoming... the male is two and the female is one. In religion, the woman is deficient: when she menstruates she does not pray and does not fast. In intellect, the woman is deficient: the testimony of a man is equal to the testimony of two women. And so on. Those who utter the word equality, if we establish this and that it is one of the rules of the Islamic Shari'ah, they must hold us to equality in these matters, or else they would be contradictory. So we say: the religion of Islam is the religion of justice, giving every person what he deserves. Indeed, the hadith says: "Overlook the faults of people of standing, except in matters of the hudud (prescribed punishments)" [Abu Dawud (4375) and an-Nasa'i (7253) from the hadith of 'A'ishah]. That is, if a dignified, noble person errs in matters other than the hudud, preserve his dignity and overlook it for him. Your overlooking it for one of the noble is a greater education than lashing him a thousand lashes, because, as it is said: "If you honour the noble, he becomes yours." But if a wicked, shameless transgressor comes, then be severe with him in punishment and discipline him. For this reason, when wine-drinking increased in the time of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, what did he do? He doubled the punishment: instead of forty, he made it eighty [Muslim (1707/38) from the hadith of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib].

Likewise, the authentic hadith related by the compilers of the Sunan: "If anyone drinks, then lash him. Then if he drinks again, lash him. Then if he drinks again, lash him. Then if he drinks—meaning—the fourth time, kill him" [Abu Dawud (4483) and an-Nasa'i (5661) from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar and a group of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ)]. Because this (punishment) has no benefit; we punish him three times but there is no benefit. So it is better for him and for others that what? That he be killed. If we kill him, he is relieved of sin, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And let not those who disbelieve think that Our giving them respite is good for them. We only give them respite that they may increase in sin; and for them is a humiliating punishment﴾ [Al 'Imran: 178].

Summary: is the expression that the religion of Islam is a religion of equality wrong or correct?

* Students: Wrong.

* The Shaykh: Wrong. What is the correct one?

* Students: A religion of justice.

* The Shaykh: A religion of justice, without doubt.

It is strange that those who say this statement also say that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There is no superiority of an Arab over a non-Arab except by piety" [al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat (4749) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id]. Thus they contradict themselves. The hadith did not negate it absolutely; it said "except by piety." So they differ by piety, or do they not differ? They differ. Moreover, I think this hadith is not authentically from the Prophet (peace be upon him), because he said: "Indeed Allah chose Kinanah from the descendants of Isma'il, and chose Quraysh from Kinanah, and chose Bani Hashim from Quraysh, and chose me from Bani Hashim" [Muslim (2276/1) from the hadith of Wathilah ibn al-Asqa'], which indicates superiority. And there is no doubt for us that the Arabs—I mean the Arab race—are superior to the race of non-Arabs. There is no doubt for us in this. The evidence for this is that Allah placed in the Arabs the most perfect prophethood and message: who? Muhammad (ﷺ). Allah placed the most perfect prophethood and message among the Arabs, and Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-An'am: 124]. Thus races differ. And the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The best of you in the Jahiliyyah are the best of you in Islam" [Agreed upon: al-Bukhari (3374) and Muslim (2378/168) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah]. Beware of following the expressions that come from the modern innovators, until you reflect on them and on what they contain of suggestions that indicate corruptions, even in the long term.

We ask Allah to guide me and you to the straight path, and to take us as His allies in this world and the Hereafter, indeed He is Able to do all things.

* * *

﴿Not equal among you are those who spent and fought before the conquest. Those are greater in rank than those who spent afterward and fought﴾ [al-Hadid: 10]. That is: they are not equal. The one who spent before the conquest. The conquest (al-fath) here refers to the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyyah, which took place between the Prophet (ﷺ) and the Quraysh, in Dhu al-Qa'dah of the sixth year after the Hijrah. It was called a conquest (fath) because it brought expansion to the Muslims and also expansion to the polytheists. People mixed with one another and people became secure from one another, until Allah the Mighty and Majestic facilitated that the Quraysh broke the treaty. After that came the greatest conquest, the conquest of Makkah in the eighth year after the Hijrah, in Ramadan.

Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Those are greater in rank than those who spent afterward and fought﴾. That is because the first ones spent and fought and preceded others to Islam, and Islam was in need of them and of their spending. So they were better than those who spent and fought afterward. Allah, glory be to Him, rewards with justice among His servants. But since the preference of the foremost might be understood to mean that the later ones have no merit, He said: ﴿And to each Allah has promised the best﴾ [al-Hadid: 10]. Each of those who spent before the conquest and fought, and those who spent afterward and fought, Allah has promised them al-husna, meaning Paradise.

﴿And Allah is Aware of what you do﴾ [al-Hadid: 10]. That is: He is Knowing of the inner aspects of your affairs as of their outer aspects; nothing is hidden from Him. And since He knows them, He will recompense every doer for what he did. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it (7). And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [az-Zalzalah: 7-8]. The conquest here is the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyyah, and al-husna means Paradise.

So all the Companions, Allah the Exalted has promised them Paradise. We testify for all the Companions that they are in Paradise, but we do not testify for any specific individual except one whom the Messenger (ﷺ) has testified for.

Then the Exalted said, urging and encouraging spending in His cause: ﴿Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan, so He will multiply it for him?﴾ [al-Hadid 11]. That is, where are those who lend Allah a goodly loan, meaning those who spend in the way He has commanded them to spend. In this, Allah points to two things: sincerity (ikhlas) and adherence to the Sunnah (muta'ah). Sincerity is indicated by His words ﴿Who is it that will lend Allah﴾, meaning that he seeks nothing but Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Adherence is indicated by His words ﴿goodly﴾, because a good deed is that which conforms to the Islamic Sharia. These two, sincerity and adherence, are the two conditions of every deed: that it be sincere to Allah, and that it follow the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in it.

Allah the Exalted described spending in His cause as a loan, by way of comparison with the loan that a person gives to another. When you lend to someone else, you are confident that he will repay you. Likewise, a righteous deed will certainly be returned to the person, and for this reason He said: ﴿so He will multiply it for him, and he will have a noble reward﴾. Multiplication here means increase. Allah, blessed and exalted, has explained its extent in Surat al-Baqarah, where He said: ﴿The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain that grows seven spikes, in each spike a hundred grains, and Allah multiplies for whom He wills﴾ [al-Baqarah 261]. So if you spend one dirham, its reward is seven hundred dirhams as a reward from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Allah's bounty is greater than His justice and more expansive, and His mercy precedes His wrath. So to how much does He multiply it for him? To seven hundred, and even more, as came in the hadith[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6491) and Muslim (131/207), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]] — to many multiples.

﴿And he will have a noble reward﴾, that is, a good and abundant reward, and that is what he will find in Paradise, where there is that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and that which has not occurred to the heart of any human being.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿The Day you will see the believing men and believing women, their light running before them and on their right hands﴾ [al-Hadid 12]. That is, mention to the nation the day when you, O human, see the believing men and believing women on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿their light running before them﴾, i.e., in front of them, ﴿and on their right hands﴾ [al-Hadid 12]. It occurs from the front and from the right. As for from the front, it is so that a person may be guided by it, since when light is in front of a person he follows it. As for from the right, it is to honor the right side, so it is before them and on their right hands.

And His saying ﴿their light running﴾ indicates that this light is in proportion to faith, because when a ruling is attached to an attribute, it is strong in the strength of that attribute and weak in its weakness.

So their light is according to their faith, not according to whether they are male or female.

﴿The Day you will see the believing men and believing women, their light running before them and on their right hands﴾. Why were "before them" and "on their right hands" specified?

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes, well done.

﴿Your glad tidings today are gardens﴾ [al-Hadid 12]. The angels say to them: ﴿your glad tidings﴾, i.e., what you are given good news of, ﴿today﴾, meaning the Day of Resurrection, ﴿gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾. These gardens contain what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived, ﴿and therein is what the souls desire and what the eyes delight in﴾ [az-Zukhruf 71]. Therein is whatever they wish, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿For them therein is whatever they wish, and with Us is more﴾ [Qaf 35]. And their collective description is that they are multiple gardens of various kinds, with different ranks according to the strength of faith and deeds.

And His saying ﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾ [al-Hadid 12]: that is, they run. "Rivers" is the plural of "river" (nahr). Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has explained in Surat Muhammad that they are four kinds: ﴿rivers of water unaltered, and rivers of milk whose taste does not change, and rivers of wine delicious to the drinkers, and rivers of purified honey﴾ [Muhammad 15]. These rivers do not need digging of channels or any lining; they flow over the surface of the earth wherever their inhabitants wish. Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

Its rivers flow without any trench, ***  Glory be to the One who holds them back from overflowing.
They do not go right or left except where its people wish.

In His saying ﴿beneath them﴾ he indicates the height of their palaces and trees, meaning these rivers are beneath these lofty palaces and tall trees.

﴿Abiding therein﴾ [al-Hadid 12]: that is, remaining therein. Multiple verses have come that this abiding is everlasting, with no cessation, no end, and no change. ﴿That is the great triumph﴾ [al-Hadid 12]. ﴿That﴾ refers to what Allah promised them, the gardens beneath which rivers flow. ﴿It is the great triumph﴾. The scholars call the word "huwa" (it/that) a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), and it serves to emphasize and restrict: that is, what has been mentioned is the great triumph, because there is no triumph like it, just as there is no greater triumph than it. We ask Allah to make us and you among its people, indeed He is Able over all things.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 57, verse 13:

﴿On the Day when the hypocrite men and hypocrite women will say to those who believed, "Wait for us that we may acquire some of your light." It will be said, "Return you backward and seek light." So a wall will be set up between them with a gate; within it is mercy, and in front of it is torment.﴾ [al-Hadid: 13].

﴿On the Day when the hypocrite men and hypocrite women will say﴾ means: remember the Day when they say. The word ﴿يَوْمَ يَقُولُ﴾ (yawma yaqulu, "on the Day when they say") is an adverb of time, and an adverb of time, place, or a prepositional phrase must have something it relates to. The scholars supply the omitted element in each context according to what fits it; here the fitting supposition is: remember, O human being, the Day when the hypocrites say, and so on.

This Day is the Day of Resurrection. The hypocrites (al-munafiqun) are those who showed Islam and concealed disbelief, ﴿They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts﴾ [al-Fath: 11]. Hypocrisy (nifaq) did not appear until the strength of the Muslims had grown after the Battle of Badr. The Battle of Badr took place in Ramadan in the second year after the Hijra, in which the Muslims won a crushing victory over the disbelievers. When the dawn of Islam broke and its strength grew, hypocrisy appeared.

Hypocrisy (nifaq) is that a person shows Islam and conceals disbelief. This spread among the Muslims, so they would come to prayer with the people and attend the congregation, but it was burdensome to them. The heaviest prayers for the hypocrites were the 'Isha' and Fajr prayers, because there were no lights in which they could be seen, and they only prayed to be seen by the people.

On the Day of Resurrection a light will appear for the believers and the hypocrites, then the light of the hypocrites will be extinguished. You, O human being, know that the extinguishing of light after it has existed is darker than if there had been no light at all, is it not so? For this reason, if you extinguish a strong light and then open your eyes, you will see nothing until after a while of time. So the extinguishing of light after its existence will be harder on them than if there had been no light there, and then their regret will be greater.

So the hypocrites will say to the believers: ﴿Wait for us﴾, look at us, ﴿that we may acquire some of your light﴾, meaning, that we may take a little of it, in the measure of need. ﴿It will be said, "Return you backward"﴾, and this "it will be said" is either from the believers or from the angels; we do not know, and God knows best.

﴿It will be said, "Return you backward and seek light"﴾. Is this literal, or is it mockery of them? That is, is it truly that they want to go back to the place where the light was extinguished, perhaps the light will be renewed there, or is it a form of ridicule and derision toward them? The verse allows both of these meanings.

Then ﴿a wall will be set up between them﴾, that is, between the hypocrites and the believers, ﴿with a gate﴾. This wall is a great wall that prevents passage over it from behind; ﴿with a gate﴾ through which the believers enter and from which the hypocrites are prevented.

﴿Within it is mercy﴾: the inside of this wall contains mercy for the believers, ﴿and in front of it is torment﴾ for the hypocrites. You cannot imagine this state, because the state is greater than we can imagine; it is a tremendous state.

﴿They will call out to them﴾ [Al-Hadid: 14]. Who is the caller? The hypocrites. And who is being called? The believers. ﴿They will call out to them: "Were we not with you?"﴾ Meaning: in the world, we were with you. We prayed with you, gave charity, and remembered Allah. ﴿They will say: "Yes"﴾. Meaning: you were with us, but only outwardly, not inwardly. That is why they say: ﴿"Yes, but you led yourselves into temptation, and you waited, and you doubted, and false hopes deceived you"﴾ [Al-Hadid: 14]. Meaning: you led yourselves astray. ﴿And you waited﴾: you awaited misfortunes to befall us, because the hypocrites wait for misfortunes to befall the believers. ﴿And you doubted﴾: you were skeptical about the matter, and you had no faith. ﴿And false hopes deceived you﴾: you thought that you were doing good. This is because they say: ﴿"We intended only good and reconciliation"﴾ [An-Nisa: 62], meaning we seek to reconcile between the believers and the disbelievers, and between faith and disbelief. ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 14], meaning they are with the believers. ﴿And when they go back to their devils, they say, "Indeed we are with you"﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 14], meaning they are with the disbelievers. They thought that by this duplicity they would win the battle, so false hopes deceived them. ﴿Until there came the command of Allah﴾ [Al-Hadid: 14], the command of Allah the Exalted, which is their death.

﴿And the Deceiver (al-Gharur) deceived you about Allah﴾. Al-Gharur is Satan. The evidence for this is the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted is He, about him when Satan whispered to our parents: Allah said of him: ﴿So he brought them down by deception﴾ [Al-A'raf: 22]. Thus, al-Gharur is Satan.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 57, verse 15:

﴿Until there comes the command of Allah, and the Deceiver deceived you concerning Allah.﴾ [al-Hadid: 14] ﴿So today no ransom will be taken from you﴾ [al-Hadid: 15]. Allah is the One whose help is sought. A prisoner in this world may ransom himself and give up wealth, and so be freed; but in the Hereafter there is no ransom. ﴿So today no ransom will be taken from you﴾, O hypocrites.

﴿Nor from those who disbelieved﴾ [al-Hadid: 15]. Those who openly declared disbelief and were bolder than these hypocrites. So there is no ransom, neither from these nor to these.

﴿Your abode is the Fire﴾ [al-Hadid: 15], that is, your dwelling place and your final destination is the Fire. ﴿It is your protector (mawlakum)﴾, the one you take as a protector, and which takes you as its own. They take the Fire as a protector by doing the deeds of its people, and the Fire takes them as its own because they deserve it. ﴿And wretched is the destination﴾ [al-Hadid: 15], that is, the place of return. This is said to disparage it. May Allah protect us and you from it. We ask Allah to make me and you among those who are distanced from the Fire and admitted into Paradise, and among the successful, the God-fearing, and the prosperous.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 57, verse 16:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Has the time not come for those who believe that their hearts should humble themselves to the remembrance of Allah and to what has descended of the truth?﴾ [al-Hadid 16]. It means: Has it not become due for these believers ﴿that their hearts should humble themselves to the remembrance of Allah﴾, i.e., that they should be abased and submit in the utmost submission to the remembrance of Allah the Exalted, in the hearts, the tongue and the limbs.

﴿And to what has descended of the truth﴾ means the Noble Quran. It is part of the remembrance of Allah, but He mentioned it specifically because of its importance.

﴿And let them not be﴾ means: and that they should not be ﴿like those who were given the Scripture before, and the term grew long for them, so their hearts became hardened, and many of them are defiant transgressors﴾ [al-Hadid 16]. Those who were given the Scripture before are the Jews and the Christians. ﴿The term grew long for them﴾ means: the time lengthened upon them, and they forgot a portion of what they had been reminded of. ﴿Their hearts became hardened﴾, may Allah protect us. ﴿And many of them are defiant transgressors﴾, though some of them are upright.

In this noble verse, Allah, blessed and exalted, makes clear that it has become due for the believers that their hearts should humble themselves to the remembrance of Allah and to the Book of Allah, and that they should not be like those who were given the Scripture before, for whom the term grew long so their hearts hardened; this is because they were distant from the era of the messages. In this there is an indication that the first of this Ummah is better than its last, and humbler in heart, because of their proximity to the era of the Message. This is confirmed by the hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: «The best of people are my generation, then those who follow them, then those who follow them»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2652) and Muslim (2533 / 212), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.]].

In this there is a complete condemnation of the Jews and the Christians, because their hearts hardened when the term grew long for them.

In it is also complete justice in the judgment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, where He said: ﴿and many of them are defiant transgressors﴾ [al-Hadid 16], and did not generalize. This is what is obligatory for one who speaks about a people: to clarify the reality. For some people, when they see deviation among some of a group, they apply the judgment to all of them. What is obligatory is justice: if the majority are the defiant transgressors, he says "most of them"; if many of them are defiant transgressors but not the majority, he uses "many", according to what the situation requires; for it is obligatory that a person speak with justice, even against himself, his parents and his relatives.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 57, verse 17:

Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿Know that Allah gives life to the earth after its death. We have certainly made the signs clear to you, so that you may understand.﴾ [al-Hadid 17].

﴿Know﴾ is an imperative verb commanding knowledge of this important matter: that Allah gives life to the earth after its death. That is, you find the earth dry, with no vegetation in it; then Allah sends down rain upon it, and it grows green, comes alive, and flourishes. When we know this, and we are aware of it because we witness it, we take it as evidence for the power of Allah, blessed and exalted, to bring the dead back to life. People are alive now, then they die, then they will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection. The One who is able to revive the earth after its death is able to revive bodies after their death, for the purpose of reckoning and recompense.
