For it is not wise for Allah, blessed and exalted, to create creatures and command them and forbid them, and to make lawful the blood of those who do not respond and their wealth, and then for the outcome to be that a person simply dies.

Rather, brothers, there must be a life which is the true life, as the Almighty said: ﴿And indeed, the Last Abode—that is the (true) Life﴾ [al-'Ankabut 64]. The meaning of ﴿al-Hayawan﴾ is: the true life after which there is no death. By al-Hayawan is not meant the animals, the beasts; what is meant by ﴿al-Hayawan﴾ is: the complete and perfect life.

You now see the earth dry, without a single green leaf; then Allah sends the rain, and it grows green, comes alive, and flourishes. The One who is able to make these dry twigs green and growing is able to give life to the dead. And in one word, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But it will be only one shout, and at once they will be upon the surface of the earth﴾ [al-Nazi'at 13, 14], and the Almighty said: ﴿It will be but one shout, and at once they will all be brought before Us﴾ [Ya-Sin 53], and ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin 82].

﴿We have certainly made the signs clear to you﴾ [al-Hadid 17]: that is, We have made them manifest to you. The signs (ayat) are the indications that point to the perfection of Allah's power, glory be to Him, and the perfection of His mercy. Let me give you an example: when Allah sends down rain, the earth grows green, the livestock are satisfied, and the atmosphere becomes pleasant. What are these the effects of? They are the effects of His mercy. We take this as evidence for Allah's mercy. And we take what Allah has created in the universe, such as the sun, the moon and the stars, and what Allah has created on the earth, such as mountains, rivers and other things, as evidence for the perfection of Allah's wisdom, the Almighty; for when you reflect upon them, you find in them such wisdom as dazzles the intellect.

So, al-ayat is the plural of ayah, which means a sign: the indications that point to the perfection of Allah's power, the Almighty, and His authority.

﴿So that you may understand﴾ [al-Hadid 17]: here (la'alla, "so that") expresses causation (ta'lil), not hope (raja'), although in the Arabic language it very often comes for hope. But here it is for causation, because hope cannot be attributed to Allah; hope is the seeking of something which involves some difficulty, whereas hope cannot be conceived with respect to Allah. Rather, la'alla here means "in order that": that you may understand. The intended understanding here is the understanding of guidance (aql al-rushd), that is, you understand with an understanding by which you are guided, and which serves as evidence for you of what contains good.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 57, verse 18:

﴿Indeed, the men who give charity and the women who give charity, and those who lend to Allah a good loan, it will be multiplied for them, and theirs will be a generous reward.﴾ [al-Hadid: 18].

﴿Indeed, the men who give charity [al-mussaddiqin]﴾: its original form is (inna al-mutasaddiqin), but the taa' was changed into a saad due to a morphological reason well known among the grammarians. That is, indeed the men who give charity and the women who give charity.

﴿And lend to Allah a good loan﴾: meaning, spend in the way of Allah with a good spending. And good spending, O our brothers, is that which combines two conditions:

The first: sincerity to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

The second: following the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

So the one who shows off in his spending, does he lend Allah a good loan? No. That is, a person gives charity to a poor man so that people will see him, and they say: "So-and-so gives much charity." This is one who shows off, and his charity does not benefit him and is not accepted from him, because every deed done for other than Allah is not accepted. Allah, blessed and exalted, said in a sacred hadith: "I am the most self-sufficient of partners from association. Whoever does a deed in which he associates others with Me, I abandon him and his association"[[Narrated by Muslim (2985 / 46) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.]]. Another person began to worship Allah with acts of worship that are not prescribed, a person of innovation, yet he is sincere. If you ask him: "Why did you do this?" he says: "I want Allah's reward, I want to draw near to Allah."

Does the worship benefit him? No. Why? Because of the lack of following.

So the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿and lend to Allah a good loan﴾ [al-Hadid: 18] means: sincere to Allah in it, following the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Here is a question: ﴿lend to Allah﴾ — is Allah poor that He should borrow?! Far from it, He is not poor. ﴿Allah has heard the statement of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 181]. So how does He say, "lend to Allah"? He says this, may He be exalted, to make clear that their reward is guaranteed just as a loan is guaranteed. If I lend someone a thousand riyals, it is established in his obligation and he must repay me. Likewise, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made worship of Him in the position of a loan, meaning that it is guaranteed; it will be returned to you. A good deed is rewarded tenfold up to seven hundred times up to many multiples.

But how can one be repaid tenfold when this would be riba in a loan? How is this so?

The answer: First, there is no riba between the servant and his Lord.

Second, in a loan, if the borrower gives you something without a condition, it is permissible. That is, if he borrows a thousand riyals from you and returns a thousand and a hundred without a condition, it is permissible, because the Prophet ﷺ borrowed a young camel (bikr, meaning a young camel) and returned something better than it, and said: "The best of you are those who are best in repaying"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2305) and Muslim (1601 / 120) with the wording "Indeed the best of you are those best in repayment" from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.]]. Did the lender benefit or not? He benefited, but he benefited without a condition. For this reason you find the jurists' phrase: (every condition that brings benefit to the lender is riba). Notice "every condition," and they did not say "every increase."

So the main point now: if someone says: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, rewards a good deed tenfold up to seven hundred times up to many multiples, and Allah has named spending in His way a loan, how can it be valid that He rewards a good deed with ten times up to seven hundred times? We say: the answer is in two respects:

First: there is no riba between the servant and his Lord.

Second: that an increase which is not a condition is permissible, and this indicates the generosity of the one who repays.

﴿It will be multiplied for them﴾ [al-Hadid: 18]: this is the predicate of (inna), meaning ﴿Indeed, the men who give charity and the women who give charity, and those who lend to Allah a good loan, it will be multiplied for them﴾, that is, their reward is given multiplied: tenfold up to seven hundred times up to many multiples.

﴿And theirs will be a generous reward﴾: that is, a noble reward. And "generous" (karim) is the good and pure. That is because Paradise contains what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.

This is "generous," and the root of karam is goodness. The evidence for this is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ to Mu'adh ibn Jabal when he sent him to Yemen: he said to him: "Beware of the choice (karaim) of their wealth," meaning: when you take zakat, avoid the choice wealth, that is, its best "and fear the supplication of the oppressed, for there is no barrier between it and Allah"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1496) and Muslim (19 / 31) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]].

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And those who believe in Allah and His messengers—those are the truthful (aṣ-ṣiddīqūn), and the martyrs with their Lord; they will have their reward and their light. But those who disbelieve and deny Our signs—those are the companions of Hellfire.﴾ [al-Ḥadīd 19].

﴿And those who believe in Allah and His messengers﴾: Belief in Allah encompasses four things:

First: belief in His existence.

Second: belief in His lordship (rubūbiyyah).

Third: belief in His divinity (ulūhiyyah).

Fourth: belief in His names and attributes.

No one denies the existence of Allah except one who is obstinate in reality; no one denies it from his heart at all. For every person knows that this ordered, firmly established universe must have a Creator and Organizer. Who is the Creator and Organizer? Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Every person also knows that no one among the human beings can control this universe. Who brings the night while the day exists? Who brings the day while the night exists? No one can.

So every sensible person believes in his heart, even if he denies with his tongue, in the existence of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. The reason is that this great creation must have a Manager.

If someone says: "It came into being by chance"? Fine, who brought it? Moreover, something that comes by chance is not organized.

If someone says: "It created itself"? We say: this too is impossible by reason. How could it create itself while it was non-existent?! This is not possible. Therefore it must have a Creator. For this reason Allah, Exalted, said in Surat al-Wāqiʿah: ﴿Have you considered the semen you emit? Is it you who create it, or are We the Creators?﴾ [al-Wāqiʿah 58-59]. Indeed, our Lord, we cannot create; a human being can never create a fetus in his mother's womb. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿O mankind, a parable has been presented, so listen to it﴾ [al-Ḥajj 73]. "Listen" (istamiʿ)—﴿O mankind﴾ is an address to all people, the disbeliever and the believer. ﴿A parable has been presented, so listen to it.﴾ Therefore, when you recite the verse, you must listen. ﴿Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah﴾, all of them, ﴿will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for it﴾ [al-Ḥajj 73]. This contemptible fly—they cannot create it even if they all gathered for it. All the worshipped beings cannot create a fly, which is among the smallest and weakest and most insignificant of animals. Furthermore, ﴿And if the fly should snatch away from them a thing, they could not retrieve it from it﴾ [al-Ḥajj 73]. That is: if the fly took anything from these idols, they could not rescue it from them.

The scholars said: the meaning is that if a fly landed on one of these idols and sucked from the perfume in it—for they used to perfume their idols—the idols could not rescue it. ﴿Weak are the seeker and the sought﴾ [al-Ḥajj 73].

I say again: no one can deny from the depths of his heart the existence of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ever; because it is agreed upon by sensible people that every occurrence must have an originator, and no one originates this universe except Allah, Mighty and Majestic. This is the first.

The second: belief in His lordship, that is, that He alone is the Creator, the Owner, and the Manager of all affairs. He is Allah alone, the Creator, the Owner, the Manager of all affairs. There is no creator but Allah, no manager of the universe but Allah, and no owner of the universe but Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Even a person's ownership of what is in his hand is not true ownership. The proof: he cannot dispose of what is in his hand as he wishes. Now, this is my pen, and it is mine, isn't it? But I do not have the right to do with it as I wish. If I wanted to burn it or break it, I would be prevented; it is forbidden to me by the Law, because the Prophet ﷺ forbade wasting property.[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhārī (1477) and Muslim (593/12) from al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah.]]

So a person's ownership of what is in his hand is not true ownership; rather, it is only that he has exclusive right to it over others.

The third: that He alone is the sole Manager of affairs. No one can ever manage affairs. Is worshipping idols right or wrong? Wrong. The idols themselves are called gods; are they the true God? No, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿That is because Allah is the Truth, and what they invoke besides Him is falsehood﴾ [al-Ḥajj 62].

So divinity means that you believe there is no god but Allah, that is, no one truly worthy of worship except Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and whatever is worshipped besides Him is false. Therefore, worship is not to be directed to anyone except Allah.

The fourth: belief in the names and attributes, His names and His attributes.

Does Allah have names? Yes. Does He have attributes? Yes. His names are the most beautiful. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And to Allah belong the most beautiful names﴾ [al-Aʿrāf 180]. His attributes are likewise sublime; there is no attribute of deficiency in them. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿For those who do not believe in the Hereafter is the description of evil, and to Allah belongs the highest description﴾ [al-Naḥl 60], that is, the highest attribute.

So we must believe in the names of Allah and believe in the attributes of Allah.

The names of Allah, Exalted, are many; it is impossible to enumerate them however much you wish; they cannot be counted. The proof is the hadith of ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd—memorize it, for it is beneficial—that: "No person is afflicted by distress, grief, or sorrow and then says: 'O Allah, I am Your servant, the son of Your servant, the son of Your female servant; my forelock is in Your hand, Your judgment over me is executed, Your decree concerning me is just. I ask You, O Allah, by every name that is Yours, which You named Yourself with, or revealed in Your Book, or taught to any of Your creation, or kept to Yourself in the knowledge of the unseen with You.'"[[Narrated by Aḥmad (3712) from Ibn Masʿūd.]]

So Allah has divided the names into three categories: those He revealed in His Book, such as al-Raḥmān; those He taught to one of His creation, such as al-Rabb and al-Shāfī. These are not in the Qur'an but came in the Sunnah. The Prophet ﷺ said: "The siwāk is a purifier of the mouth and a pleasing thing to the Lord";[[Narrated by al-Nasāʾī (5) and al-Dārimī (711) from ʿĀʾishah.]] and he ﷺ said: "As for the bowing, glorify the Lord in it";[[Narrated by Muslim (479/207) from Ibn ʿAbbās.]] this is revealed in His Book or taught to one of His creation. This is the second.

The third category: what Allah has kept to Himself in the knowledge of the unseen. "Kept to Himself" means He alone knows it; He did not reveal it in the Book and did not teach it to anyone of creation. Is it possible to comprehend it? No. So the names of Allah cannot be comprehended nor limited to a number, because we do not know them.

As for the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Indeed Allah has ninety-nine names; whoever counts them enters Paradise,"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhārī (2736) and Muslim (2677/6) from Abū Hurayrah.]] the meaning is that among the names there are ninety-nine names, and whoever counts them enters Paradise. That is the meaning. "Counting them" means knowing them verbally, understanding their meaning, and worshipping Allah according to what they require. It does not mean merely memorizing them. No, one must memorize the wording; second, understand the meaning; and third, worship Allah by them according to their requirements. For example, if you know that Allah, Exalted, is Forgiving, then expose yourself to forgiveness; do not say "Allah is Forgiving" and commit sins whenever you wish. Seek forgiveness from Allah and you will find Him Forgiving and Merciful. If you know that Allah is Mighty, worship Allah according to this, fear Him and beware of Him, and so on.

As for belief in the messengers, it includes affirming what they all reported, from the first of them to the last. We must affirm what the messengers reported, if it is authentically transmitted from them. As for acting upon their laws, we do not act, or it is not obligatory on us to act, except: first, affirming what they reported; but on the condition that it is authentically transmitted from them.

Second: acting upon the laws. But this is only by the law of Muhammad ﷺ, because his law abrogated all the previous laws. ﴿Those are the truthful (aṣ-ṣiddīqūn)﴾ [al-Ḥadīd 19]. ﴿Those﴾ refers to those who believed in Allah and His messengers; ﴿they are the truthful﴾, that is, those who attain truthfulness to a great degree, because ṣiddīq is an intensive form, and truthfulness is by intention, by speech, and by deed. As for truthfulness of intention: that a person intends by his worship the Face of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and no one else. Whoever intends by his worship something other than Allah has committed shirk, and his deed is not accepted, due to the Prophet's ﷺ saying in the sacred ḥadīth from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, that He said: "I am the most self-sufficient of partners in need of partnership; whoever does a deed in which he associates others with Me, I abandon him and his partner."[[Narrated by Muslim (2985/46) from Abū Hurayrah.]]

The second: truthfulness in speech, that a person is truthful in what he reports. Allah, Exalted, has praised the truthful and commanded us to be with them. He, Exalted, said: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah and be with the truthful﴾ [al-Tawbah 119]. He praised the emigrants who left their homes and wealth: ﴿seeking bounty from Allah and approval, and supporting Allah and His messenger; those are the truthful﴾ [al-Ḥashr 8].

The Prophet ﷺ commanded truthfulness, urged it, and encouraged it, saying: "Keep to truthfulness, for truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. A man continues to tell the truth and seek the truth until he is recorded with Allah as a ṣiddīq. Beware of lying, for lying leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire. A man continues to lie and seek lying until he is recorded with Allah as a liar (kadhdhāb)."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhārī (6094) and Muslim (2607/105) from Ibn Masʿūd.]]

As for truthfulness in deed: following the Prophet ﷺ, because whoever is truthful in his claim of loving Allah and His messenger should follow the Messenger ﷺ, due to the saying of Allah, Exalted: ﴿Say: If you should love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 31]. Some of the early scholars called this verse the "verse of the trial" (āyat al-miḥnah), meaning the test. So whoever claims that he loves Allah and His messenger, we say to him: go ahead, follow the Messenger. If he follows him, he is truthful; if he opposes him, he is not truthful.

﴿And the martyrs with their Lord; they will have their reward and their light﴾ [al-Ḥadīd 19]. ﴿And the martyrs﴾ is the plural of shahīd, and what is meant by them are those who were killed in the way of Allah. Fighting in the way of Allah means that a person fights the enemy of Allah so that the word of Allah is the highest. This is fighting in the way of Allah. The Prophet ﷺ said this when he was asked about a man who fights for bravery, fights out of tribal zeal, and fights to be seen in his position: which of these is in the way of Allah? He said: "Whoever fights so that the word of Allah is the highest, he is in the way of Allah."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhārī (7458) and Muslim (1904/150) from Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī.]] This one who fights for bravery means he loves fighting; a brave man loves to fight, like a hunter who loves to hunt. The hunter who is fond of hunting—you find him loving this, going out and enduring hardships to catch the prey, and when he catches it, it becomes cheaper in his eyes than anything.

So this one fights for bravery because he is brave and loves to fight.

"And fights out of tribal zeal" means: partisanship for his people.

"And fights to be seen in his position" means: showing off, as in the other wording: "and fights for show." He said: "Whoever fights so that the word of Allah is the highest, he is in the way of Allah." Does one who fights to recover his usurped land do so in the way of Allah, or out of zeal? Out of zeal, unless he says: "I want to recover it in order to establish the rites of Islam upon it"—then this is in the way of Allah. But whoever fights because this is his land and he wants it returned to him, this is zeal; he does not have the reward of the martyrs if he is killed.

These are martyrs: ﴿for them is their reward and their light﴾, that is, their great reward, as Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And never think of those who have been killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision. Rejoicing in what Allah has given them of His bounty, and they rejoice for those who have not yet joined them from behind them—that there is no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve. They rejoice in favor from Allah and bounty, and that Allah does not allow the reward of the believers to be lost﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 169-171].

﴿For them is their reward and their light.﴾ When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned the companions of the right and their reward, He then mentioned the companions of the left: ﴿And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs—those are the companions of Hellfire﴾ [al-Ḥadīd 19]. This is because the Qur'an is mathānī (oft-repeated); matters and meanings are repeated within it. For this reason, you find that when the Qur'an mentions Paradise, it usually mentions the Fire, and when it mentions the friends of Allah, it mentions the enemies of Allah. The wisdom in this is that a person does not become bored, since whenever the meaning moves to another meaning, the person becomes energized.

Another wisdom: that a person journeys toward Allah—that is, worships Allah—between fear and hope. When the attributes of the believers are mentioned, or pass by him, the aspect of hope is strengthened; and when the conditions of the disbelievers are mentioned, the aspect of fear prevails. For this reason He said: ﴿And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs﴾. He conjoined denial (takdhīb) to disbelief (kufr), which is a type of it, but because it is more severe—one who disbelieves but does not deny is less culpable than one who denies. So ﴿and denied Our signs﴾ is conjoined to ﴿disbelieved﴾ by the conjunction of the specific to the general, like the conjoining of Gabriel (al-rūḥ) to the angels, though he is one of them. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein﴾ [al-Qadr 4]; "the Spirit" is Gabriel, and he is among the angels.

﴿And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs—those are the companions of al-Jaḥīm.﴾ Al-Jaḥīm is a name of the Fire, and "companions" (aṣḥāb) means those who are constantly bound to it. Therefore, whenever a verse containing "companions" (aṣḥāb) passes by you, the meaning is that they are constantly bound to it and abide in it forever. We ask Allah for well-being.

In the first verses there is encouragement toward the qualities that lead to the Gardens, because Allah, Exalted, did not mention these matters for us merely to be informed of them, but so that we would strive for them. And there is in them a warning against disbelief and denial, lest a person fall into this painful punishment: ﴿those are the companions of al-Jaḥīm.﴾

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 57, verse 20:

﴿Know that the life of this world is﴾ ... to the end of the verse [al-Hadid: 20]. When Allah mentioned the conditions of the believers and the conditions of the disbelievers, who in this world each act according to his own manner, He explained the reality of the world, what it is, and commanded us to know it, so that a person would strive in reflection and contemplation. The command to know something that is established means that you are required to reflect much until the matter becomes clear to you.

﴿Know that the life of this world is﴾, that is, this life of ours, ﴿mere play and diversion, adornment and boasting among yourselves, and rivalry in wealth and children﴾. Five things: play of the limbs, and diversion of the hearts.

As for play of the limbs, it is a person doing deeds that turn him away from the remembrance of Allah and from the prayer.

As for diversion of the hearts, it is heedlessness, and this is more severe and greater: heedlessness of the heart. May Allah protect us and you from it and give life to our hearts and yours. Heedlessness is great; it deprives you of all the pleasures of acts of obedience and bars you from all their effects. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance and who follows his desire﴾ [al-Kahf: 28]. He did not say: "Do not obey one whose tongue We have silenced," but said: ﴿whose heart We have made heedless﴾ [al-Kahf: 28]. How much remembrance there is with the tongue alongside heedlessness of the heart! This undoubtedly diminishes the reward and diminishes the effects that follow from remembrance, such as the goodness of the heart, turning toward Allah, returning to Him, and other things.

﴿Play and diversion﴾: play is in the limbs, and diversion is in the hearts.

﴿And adornment﴾: yes, adornment in clothing, adornment in vehicles, adornment in dwellings, adornment in everything. For this reason you will find a person, even if he is poor, loves to adorn his home with decoration and the like, and likewise his car. Among us there are couples: when the husband wants to ride a car, he places on it garlands of flowers and other things, as adornment.

﴿And boasting among yourselves﴾: each one boasts over the other: "I am from such-and-such tribe and you are from such-and-such tribe; your tribe is worth nothing in society, and my tribe is an exalted tribe." They boast. There is boasting in knowledge: one has knowledge of medicine and another does not know about medicine; this one's knowledge is in engineering and that one does not know, so he boasts over him. Even more repugnant than that is boasting with religious knowledge, because religious knowledge obliges a person, when he acquires it and Allah bestows it upon him, to become more humble and to know himself and his own worth.

﴿And boasting among yourselves﴾: among what occurs in this is what happens between poets at times, in insults toward others and boasting, as is found at some celebrations and occasions, of what we hear.

﴿And boasting among yourselves and rivalry in wealth and children﴾: rivalry, each one loves to be greater in wealth and greater in children. This is like His saying: ﴿Adorned for mankind is the love of desires: women and children, and heaped-up piles of gold and silver, and branded horses, and cattle, and tilth. That is the enjoyment of the life of this world﴾ [Al 'Imran: 14]. This is the reality of the world. Yet, with this diversion, play, boasting, and adornment, does it remain? Never. It does not remain; it must vanish. When a person's lifespan lengthens, he returns to decrepitude. On this the poet says:

There is no pleasure in life while its delights are troubled
by the remembrance of death and old age.

Every person, when he reflects on his life and that he is in bliss, says: "And what comes after that? What is after it?" Either death or decrepitude: either you die and leave the world, or you grow old and become a burden on your son and daughter, and even your family grow weary of you. For this reason Allah, Mighty and Majestic, pointed to this state and said: ﴿If one of them or both of them reach old age with you, do not say to them, "Uff"﴾ [al-Isra: 23], because when they reach old age their thinking becomes disordered and they become weary. So you will either die or reach the state of decrepitude, if the world remains for you; otherwise you may be stripped of it before you reach decrepitude and before you die.

So from this we take caution against the trial of the world. How many a person has been made insolent by the life of this world and perished! In the sacred hadith: "Among My servants is one whom, if I make him wealthy, wealth will corrupt him"[[Al-Asma' wa al-Sifat by al-Bayhaqi (1/307), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]]. Indeed the Prophet ﷺ said: "By Allah, it is not poverty that I fear for you; rather I fear that the world will be opened to you, and you will compete for it as those before you competed for it, and it will destroy you as it destroyed them"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4015) and Muslim (2961/6), from the hadith of 'Amr ibn 'Awf.]]. The Messenger ﷺ spoke the truth. Most of the corrupt, most of the disbelievers, are from whom? From the elite and the wicked. Read the Qur'an: who denies the messengers? The elite and the wicked. Take heed from reality now: what corrupts the world most are the wealthy and the rich upon whom the world has been opened. So let the wise and intelligent person beware of it, and let him limit himself from it to what benefits him in the Hereafter. This is the reality of the world.

Then Allah struck a parable for it, because parables bring meanings close, for a parable means measuring the meaning against the perceptible: ﴿like the example of rain whose vegetation pleases the disbelievers﴾. "Rain" means water by which the earth brings forth growth and by which hardship is removed. ﴿Whose vegetation pleases the disbelievers﴾ means the vegetation that arises from it; "pleases" means they find it good. "The disbelievers" are those who disbelieve in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because the disbeliever is pleased by the world, rejoices in it, is delighted by it, and his heart is attached to it; he has no concern except what he sees of its adornment and diversion. So he is one whom ﴿the disbelievers﴾ are pleased by, that is, the disbelievers in Allah.

﴿Its vegetation﴾, that is, the vegetation of this rain. Why did He specify the disbelievers? I told you: because the disbelievers are the ones who find the world good and are impressed by it, and their hearts are attached to it. As for the believers, they are the opposite; they are concerned only with what serves the interest of the Hereafter.

It has been said that what is meant by "the disbelievers" here is the farmers, but this is not correct, because applying "disbelievers" to farmers is extremely rare, if it is even valid. Those who say that what is meant is the farmers say: because the farmer "covers" (kafara) the seed, that is, he buries it in the earth, tilling the land over it so that it will sprout. But what we have established first is the correct view: that what is meant by "the disbelievers" is the disbelievers in Allah.

﴿Its vegetation pleases the disbelievers; then﴾ after it appears and pleases the disbelievers, they find it good and marvel at it, ﴿it dries up﴾, that is, it withers and becomes dry, ﴿so you see it turned yellow﴾, after it was green and growing it becomes yellow, ﴿then it becomes debris﴾, meaning it shatters and breaks into pieces, because it has dried out. So what was the outcome of this crop? Ruin and disappearance. This is the state of the world: it displays to a person its bliss, its palaces, its vehicles, its wealth, its children, its wives, and other things, and suddenly it shatters.

How many a wealthy person was joyful with his family, blessed in his house, in his vehicle, in his clothing, and in all his circumstances, and then he returns poor! His world is shattered. If he has not died, and his world has been shattered by his separation from this world, then there must be one of two things: either the world leaves you, or you leave it. This is the state of the world, and this is a matter that is not doubted in reality. But souls are heedless, and a person forgets such an established matter, so he thinks that everything is fine and considers the world's ending or his own departure from it far off.

As for the Hereafter, listen to it. He says: ﴿And in the Hereafter is severe punishment﴾ for the disbelievers, ﴿and forgiveness from Allah and approval﴾ for the believers. So which is more deserving: that a person prefer the world, whose end is annihilation and cessation, or the Hereafter? The second: he prefers the Hereafter. This is sound reason, because if you prefer the world, in the Hereafter there is severe punishment, and if you prefer the Hereafter, in it there is forgiveness from Allah and approval: forgiveness of sins and approval for good deeds. ﴿And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion﴾. This sentence contains restriction (hasr), its method being negation and affirmation, and it is the highest method of restriction: the life of this world is nothing but enjoyment, nothing else; and the enjoyment of delusion is that a person is deceived by it, so he amuses himself, plays, rejoices, and becomes arrogant, and then it vanishes.

All these sentences and these descriptions, Allah the Mighty and Majestic intends—and He knows best—that a person should renounce the world and desire the Hereafter.

And I ask you: whoever renounces the world and desires the Hereafter, does he miss anything of the world's bliss?

The answer: No, he does not miss it, even if he becomes poor; he does not miss the world's bliss. The evidence for this from the Qur'an and the Sunnah is that Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer—We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾ [al-Nahl: 97]. He did not say: "We will increase his wealth, his children, and his palaces," but ﴿We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾, tranquil, with his mind at ease ﴿and We will surely give them their reward according to the best of what they used to do﴾ [al-Nahl: 97]. The Prophet ﷺ explained this in his saying: "How wondrous is the affair of the believer! Indeed all his affairs are good, and this is not so for anyone except the believer: if adversity afflicts him, he is patient, and that is good for him; and if ease afflicts him, he is thankful, and that is good for him."[[Narrated by Muslim (2999/64) from the hadith of Suhayb.]]

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Race to forgiveness from your Lord﴾ [al-Hadid 21]. "Sabiqu" is a command to compete, and in another verse the command comes as "musara'a" (hastening). So a person combines al-musabaqa (competing, which is running at full speed while walking) with al-musara'a (hastening to do good).

﴿to forgiveness from your Lord﴾ [al-Hadid 21]: this is by doing the things that bring forgiveness.

Among the causes of forgiveness: that you ask Allah for forgiveness. You say, "O Allah, forgive me," or you say, "I seek Allah's forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance."

And among the causes of forgiveness: doing what brings forgiveness, such as the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever fasts Ramadan out of faith and seeking reward, Allah will forgive him his previous sins" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (38) and Muslim (760 / 175) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah]. And like the saying of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, regarding the one who performs ablution and perfects it, then prays two rak'ahs without letting his mind wander during them: "Allah will forgive him his previous sins" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (159) and Muslim (226 / 3) from the hadith of Uthman ibn Affan].

And like his saying ﷺ: "Whoever says 'Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi' (Glory be to Allah and praise Him) one hundred times, his sins will be forgiven, even if they were like the foam of the sea" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6405) and Muslim (2691 / 28) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah]. Examples of this are many. The point is that racing to forgiveness means: what brings forgiveness, whether asking for forgiveness directly, as when you say, "O Allah, forgive me," or doing what brings forgiveness, such as fasting Ramadan out of faith and seeking reward, as in: "Whoever fasts Ramadan out of faith and seeking reward, Allah will forgive him his previous sins." Charity also extinguishes sin just as water extinguishes fire.

﴿and a Garden whose width﴾ [al-Hadid 21]: al-Jannah (the Garden) is the abode of bliss that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, prepared for the God-fearing. In it is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. In it are fruits, date palms, pomegranates, couches, honey, milk, and other things. But do you think that what is in it resembles what is in this world?

The answer: No, do not think this, because Allah says: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾ [as-Sajdah 17]. There is nothing in Paradise from what is in this world except the names alone. The name "pomegranate" is used, but it differs from the pomegranate of this world; "fruit" differs from the fruit of this world; "couches" differ from the couches of this world; and so on.

Be mindful of this, and do not think that what is mentioned in Paradise by name corresponds in reality to what is in this world. This is impossible, because of what you heard in the verse: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾, and in the sacred hadith: "I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3244) and Muslim (2824 / 2) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah].

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿a Garden whose width is like the width of the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Hadid 21]. In Surat Ali 'Imran: ﴿whose width is the heavens and the earth﴾ [Ali 'Imran 133]. There is no contradiction, because the first, "its width is like the width of the heavens," is a simile, and the second, "its width is the heavens and the earth," is also a simile; but the people of rhetoric call it a complete (balagh) simile.

﴿like the width of the heavens and the earth﴾: who can estimate the width of the heavens and the earth? No one can. The heavens in their vastness: the lowest heaven is extremely wide. How great is the distance between it and the earth? It encompasses the earth. The second heaven is above it and is wider, and the third is wider still, and so on, until you reach the Kursi (Footstool). The Prophet ﷺ said about the Kursi: "The seven heavens and the seven earths, compared to the Kursi, are no more than a ring thrown into a desert of the earth." A ring: the ring of a helmet, not the large ring of a door; the ring of a coat of mail is very small. Throw it into a desert of the earth; what is it compared to the desert? Nothing. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: "The excellence of the Throne over the Kursi is like the excellence of the desert over this ring" [Narrated by Ibn Hibban in his Sahih (361) from the hadith of Abu Dharr].

So who can grasp the width of the heavens and the earth? No one can. The Garden's width is like the width of the heavens and the earth. For this reason, the least of the people of Paradise in rank is one who looks at his kingdom from a distance of two thousand years, and sees its farthest part as he sees its nearest. Allah mentioned that its width is the width of the heavens and the earth so that we would be eager to fill this land, the land of Paradise.

In a hadith, Ibrahim, peace be upon him, said to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace: "Convey my greetings of peace to your Ummah, and inform them that Paradise is a plain (qi'an), and its planting is Subhan Allah, al-Hamdu lillah, la ilaha illa Allah, and Allahu akbar" [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (3462) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud].

So, my brother, be keen to fill what you deserve of this Garden with the remembrance of Allah, the recitation of His Book, and other things that bring you closer to Allah.

For whom is this Garden, whose width is like the width of the heavens and the earth?

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿It has been prepared for those who believe in Allah and His messengers﴾ [al-Hadid 21]. "U'iddat" (it has been prepared): who prepared it? Allah, Mighty and Majestic, prepared it, as He said: ﴿Allah has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ [at-Tawbah 89]. The meaning of i'dad (preparation) is making something ready.

﴿for those who believe in Allah and His messengers﴾: they believe in Allah and in everything that belief in Allah requires. So belief includes belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine decree, both its good and its bad.

His saying ﴿and His messengers﴾ includes all the messengers, the first of whom was Nuh and the last of whom was Muhammad. But our belief in the messengers differs from our belief in Muhammad, peace be upon him. Our belief in the messengers means that we believe they are truthful, conveying from Allah, and we believe in all that is authentically reported of their reports. As for following them, no: following applies to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace. They share with the Messenger that we believe they are truthful, that everything they reported is true, that everything they brought is just, and suited to the circumstances of their peoples in their time. As for following, we follow only one of them, Muhammad ﷺ.

His saying ﴿believe in Allah and His messengers﴾ indicates that the People of the Book, Jews and Christians, are not among the people of Paradise, because they did not believe in the messengers of Allah. The evidence is that they disbelieved in Muhammad, peace be upon him, and whoever disbelieves in one messenger disbelieves in all of them. How can that not be so, when Muhammad, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, came with the abrogation (naskh) of all previous laws? Have you not heard the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿The people of Nuh denied the messengers﴾ [ash-Shu'ara 105]? Answer!

* Students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Did any messenger precede Nuh? How can He say: ﴿The people of Nuh denied the messengers﴾?

The answer: because whoever denies one messenger has denied all the messengers. How much more so one who denies Muhammad, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, whose law abrogated all previous laws, and about whom Allah said: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: "Whatever I have given you of Scripture and wisdom, then there will come to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him"﴾ [Ali 'Imran 81]. He took the covenant of all the prophets. ﴿"Whatever I have given you of Scripture and wisdom, then there will come to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him." He said: "Do you affirm and accept My covenant on that?" They said: "We affirm"﴾ [Ali 'Imran 81]. Who is this messenger? Muhammad ﷺ. All the messengers are obliged to believe in the Messenger, peace be upon him. For this reason, on the night of the Isra' (Night Journey), who was the imam? Their imam in prayer was Muhammad, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace.

Therefore, the Jews and Christians are not among the people of Paradise after the sending of the Messenger ﷺ. Why? Because they did not believe in his messengers; they disbelieved in Muhammad. Rather, they also disbelieved in their own messengers, by the saying of Allah Most High: ﴿The people of Nuh denied the messengers﴾ [ash-Shu'ara 105].

And because 'Isa ibn Maryam, peace be upon him, gave them good news of Muhammad. In Surat as-Saff: ﴿And when 'Isa, son of Maryam, said: "O Children of Israel, I am the messenger of Allah to you, confirming what came before me of the Torah, and giving good news of a messenger who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad"﴾. When this messenger foretold by 'Isa came to them, ﴿they said: "This is clear magic"﴾ [as-Saff 6], and they disbelieved in him.

So they disbelieved in 'Isa and rejected and denied his good news. It is never permissible for us to say that the religions of the Jews and Christians today are valid religions at all. Rather, they are false religions, not accepted by Allah, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him﴾ [Ali 'Imran 85].

Returning to the verse: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿It has been prepared for those who believe in Allah and His messengers. That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills﴾ [al-Hadid 21]. ﴿That﴾ means what Allah has prepared for these believers in Allah and His messengers. ﴿The bounty of Allah﴾ in that they believed in Allah, believed in His messengers, and followed the Messenger, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, they are rewarded with these gardens. ﴿That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills.﴾ O Allah, grant us from Your bounty.

﴿which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty﴾

As for His saying ﴿which He gives to whom He wills﴾: do you think this willing is mere will? No.

It is a will joined with wisdom. That is, whoever is worthy of bounty, Allah gives him bounty, and whoever is not worthy of it, He does not give it to him. The evidence is the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-An'am 124]. He will place His message only with one who is worthy of it.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, also said: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [as-Saff 5].

And He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿But if they turn away, then know that Allah intends to afflict them for some of their sins. And indeed, many of the people are defiantly disobedient﴾ [al-Ma'idah 49].

Do not think that Allah gives bounty to whom He wills without a cause. There must be a cause. When Allah knows goodness in a person's heart, O Allah, make our hearts full of goodness, He gives him goodness. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿O Prophet, say to those prisoners in your hands: "If Allah knows goodness in your hearts, He will give you better than what was taken from you and will forgive you. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful"﴾ [al-Anfal 70]. Set your heart right between you and Allah, and you will find all goodness.

﴿And Allah is the Possessor of great bounty﴾ [al-Hadid 21]: that is, the Possessor of great bounty, Mighty and Majestic. No one is greater in favor than Allah, Exalted. He brought you into existence from nothing, sustained you and supplied you with blessings, and facilitated guidance for you and guided you to it. Who is greater in favor than Allah? No one. For this reason Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿They consider it a favor to you that they have embraced Islam. Say: "Do not consider your Islam a favor to me. Rather, Allah has conferred a favor upon you that He has guided you to faith"﴾ [al-Hujurat 17]. When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, gathered the Ansar at the battle of Hunayn, when he divided the spoils among those whose hearts were to be reconciled, he addressed them, saying: "Did I not find you astray, and Allah guided you through me?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger are most gracious." He said: "Did I not find you divided, and Allah united you through me?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger are most gracious" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4330) and Muslim (1061 / 139) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Zayd]. Whenever he said a statement, they said, "Allah and His Messenger are most gracious," meaning greater in favor.

The conclusion is that Allah, Exalted, is the Possessor of great bounty, but He gives His bounty to whoever deserves it, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And He gives every possessor of virtue his virtue﴾ [Hud 3]. O Allah, we ask You, by Your great bounty, to guide our hearts, to set right our deeds, and to end our lives with good, indeed You are capable of all things.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 57, verse 22–23:

He, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿No affliction befalls upon the earth or in yourselves except that it is in a Book before We bring it into being. Indeed, that is easy for Allah.﴾ [al-Hadid 22] This means that all the afflictions that befall a person on the earth or in himself have been written beforehand. An affliction on the earth is like drought and scarcity of rain, the sinking of water and difficulty in reaching it, and it may also be said: strife, wars, and others. ﴿Nor in yourselves﴾ means: in the person's own self, such as illness, or the loss of a beloved one, or the loss of wealth, or the like, even the thorn that pricks him.

﴿Except in a Book﴾: this Book is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), in which Allah has written the decrees of everything. "When Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, created the Pen, He said to it: 'Write.' It said: 'My Lord, what shall I write?' He said: 'Write what will be until the Day of Resurrection.' So it wrote what will be until the Day of Resurrection."[[Reported by al-Tabarani in Musnad al-Shamiyyin (1572) from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar.]] Glory be to Allah! How great is this Tablet that contains everything until the Day of Resurrection. But this is not strange regarding the power of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because the command of Allah, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is. [Ya-Sin 82] People used to be astonished before and would not consider it far-fetched. They would be astonished, but would not find it unlikely that the decrees of everything are written in this Tablet. Now there has appeared, made by human hands, a small piece in which thousands of words are recorded, is it not so?

* Students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: What is it called? Laser, disc... In any case, you know it now. It is a small plate like a disc in which thousands of words are recorded. All the published books of hadith, or all the exegeses, or all the books of the jurists may be recorded in it. It is made by human hands, so how about the making of One who says to a thing, "Be," and it is! When He said, "Write what will be until the Day of Resurrection," it wrote what will be until the Day of Resurrection. So, are the afflictions that befall people part of a prior decree or are they newly initiated?

The answer: the first. For this reason He said: ﴿except in a Book﴾, ﴿before We bring it into being﴾. Regarding the pronoun in His saying ﴿nabra'aha﴾ (We bring it into being), it has been said that it refers to affliction; it has been said that it refers to the earth; it has been said that it refers to the souls; it has been said that it refers to all of them. The correct view is that it refers to all of them, meaning: before We bring all these things into being, that is, before We create them. That is because Allah wrote the decrees of everything fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth, and fifty thousand years is a long period, and this is written.

So ﴿before We bring it into being﴾: the pronoun refers to what? To the earth? To the affliction? To the souls? To all of them? All of them.

And ﴿nabra'aha﴾ means: We create them. For how long? Fifty thousand years before Allah created the heavens and the earth.

﴿Indeed, that is easy for Allah﴾ means: the writing of these afflictions is easy for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. How is it easy? Because He said to the Pen, "Write," and it wrote. Is this easy or difficult? Easy. One word accomplished everything. ﴿Indeed, that is easy for Allah﴾: everything is easy for Allah, because His command is one word, ﴿"Be," and it is﴾ [al-Baqarah 117]. Have you seen that the creation will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection with one word? Say it, O people.

* Students: With one word.

* The Shaykh: One word. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿It will be but one shout, and behold, they will all be brought before Us﴾ [Ya-Sin 53], and He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿It will be but one shout, and at once they will be on the surface of the earth﴾ [al-Nazi'at 13–14]. That is, on the face of the earth; they will come out of the graves. This is easy, by Allah.

When Zakariyya said to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, when He gave him the good news of a son: ﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened and my head has glistened with white hair"﴾ [Maryam 4], meaning from old age, ﴿"and I have reached extreme old age"﴾ [Maryam 8]. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿"So it will be. Your Lord says: It is easy for Me, and I created you before, when you were nothing"﴾ [Maryam 9]. So I brought you into existence before you were, and by My power you will have a son after this long period.

So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is not incapable of anything, nothing defies Him, and nothing delays from His cosmic command. ﴿Indeed, that is easy for Allah. (22) So that you will not despair over what has escaped you﴾ [al-Hadid 22–23]. That is: We have informed you of this, that every affliction that occurs is in a Book, so that you do not grieve. The lam here indicates purpose, and "kay" means "an" (so that), that is, lest you grieve. The meaning of "ta'saw" is: you feel regret over what has escaped you of what you love.

﴿And do not exult in what He has given you﴾ [al-Hadid 23], that is: do not exult with arrogance and self-sufficiency apart from Allah because of what He has given you of His bounty.

If you know that a thing has been written beforehand, will you regret what has passed, since it is written, and what is written must occur? Will you exult with arrogance and self-sufficiency when Allah grants you bounty? No, because it was written by Allah beforehand. So be moderate: do not regret what has passed, and do not exult with arrogance and self-sufficiency over what Allah has granted you of His bounty, since it is from Allah. In the authentic hadith, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer." The strong is strong in his faith, not strong in his body. People of physical training make this a headline: "The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer," and they say: it means the believer who is strong in his body. This is an error. "The strong believer": "strong" here is a description referring to what precedes it, which is faith. "The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, and there is good in both." This is what the rhetoricians call *ihtiras* (a precautionary qualification), meaning that one might think the weak has no good in him, so he said: "and there is good in both." Then he said: "Be eager for what benefits you, seek help from Allah and do not be incapable. If something befalls you, do not say, 'If only I had done such and such, it would have been such and such,' but say: 'Allah decreed, and He does what He wills,' for 'if only' opens the work of Satan."[[Reported by Muslim (2664/34) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]

When a person knows that everything is decreed and must occur, he is content with what has occurred, and he knows that what has occurred can never be removed. For this reason it is said: the permanence of a state is impossible, and changing a state, meaning removing a thing after it has occurred, is impossible.

Let us return to the verse: ﴿So that you will not despair over what has escaped you and not exult in what He has given you. And Allah does not love everyone self-deluded and boastful﴾. Self-deluded (mukhtal) in his action, boastful (fakhur) in his speech. Among self-delusion in action is trailing one's garment, or one's cloak, or one's cape, or other things that indicate conceit, even if one wears a garment that is not trailing, it is still considered conceit, and so it is conceit. The boastful one is the self-admiring person who says, "I did this and I did that and I did that," boasting of it over people. Since you are doing a thing seeking Allah's reward, there is no need to boast of it to people. Rather, thank Allah for it and speak of it as a blessing of Allah upon you.
