Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 57, verse 24:

﴿Those who are stingy and enjoin stinginess upon people﴾ [al-Hadid: 24].

﴿Yabkhalun﴾ means: they withhold what is obligatory for them to give, whether of wealth, standing (jah), or knowledge.

An example of the first: one who is stingy with zakat, which is the greatest and most obligatory of expenditures, and with spending on those whose maintenance is obligatory, such as relatives and wives.

An example of the second: a person finds a Muslim who is caught in an injustice, where the situation calls for him to intercede so that this injustice may be lifted, but he is stingy. Stingy with what? With his standing.

An example of the third, which is stinginess with one's knowledge: that he refrains from teaching people what Allah the Mighty and Majestic has taught him, and that he is stingy with an answer and a fatwa when he is asked about a religious matter and it becomes incumbent upon him to issue a ruling on it. In a hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "The stingy person is the one in whose presence I am mentioned and he does not send blessings upon me" [narrated by al-Tirmidhi (3546) and al-Nasa'i (9800) from the hadith of al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Talib]. May Allah send blessings and peace upon him. This is a type of stinginess, because he is stingy with what is obligatory upon him, since the preponderant view is that when the Prophet (ﷺ) is mentioned, it is obligatory upon whoever hears him to send blessings upon him, based on the hadith in the Sunan that Jibril said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "May he be humbled into the dust, the man in whose presence I am mentioned and he does not send blessings upon you." Say: "Amin." So he said: "Amin" [narrated by al-Tirmidhi (3545) and Ahmad (7451) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah].

﴿And enjoin stinginess upon people﴾ (ya'murun): that is, these people say to a man: Do not spend from your wealth, for your wealth will decrease; do not exhaust yourself interceding for so-and-so; do not exhaust yourself teaching knowledge. These people command him to be stingy, and so they become—and we seek refuge in Allah—corrupt and corrupters.

Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And whoever turns away﴾ [al-Hadid: 24], that is, turns away from obedience to Allah, ﴿then indeed Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy﴾ [al-Hadid: 24]. Whoever turns away, Allah has no need of him. He, the Mighty and Majestic, is self-sufficient, free of need of all His creation. And He is ﴿al-Hamid﴾, that is, the One praised for His self-sufficiency, because not every self-sufficient person is praised; the self-sufficient stingy person is not praised. But Allah the Mighty and Majestic is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy, who is praised for His self-sufficiency, because He, the Mighty and Majestic, is abundant in giving and generous in bestowal.

In this verse is evidence that the person who turns away from obedience to Allah only harms himself and does not harm Allah in any way, for Allah is Free of need. In the sacred hadith: "O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were upon the most wicked heart of a single man among you, that would not decrease My dominion in the least" [narrated by Muslim (2577/55) from the hadith of Abu Dharr].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 57, verse 25 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear evidences, and sent down with them the Book and the balance that people may uphold justice. And We sent down iron, wherein is great military might and benefits for people, and that Allah may make evident who supports Him and His messengers unseen. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.﴾ [al-Hadid 25].

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear evidences﴾ is a sentence emphasized by the lam and (qad) and by an implied oath, because such a sentence is one in which an oath is implied. The implied meaning is: "By Allah, We certainly sent Our messengers with clear evidences." Perhaps one of you will say: How does Allah swear? How does Allah emphasize His report with an oath when He is the Truthful even without it? This is a point of difficulty. The answer is that it is said: the Noble Qur'an was revealed in a clear Arabic tongue, and the clear Arabic tongue emphasizes important matters or disputed matters with various kinds of emphasis, so that the addressee is reassured and the obstinate one does not persist in his obstinacy. So here we say: ﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear evidences﴾; the implied sense of the speech is: "By Allah, We certainly sent Our messengers with clear evidences." This recurs often in the Qur'an, and the implied oath is as you have heard.

﴿We sent Our messengers with clear evidences﴾, that is: We gave them the revelation and commanded them to convey it to people. This is the messenger.

And His saying: ﴿with clear evidences﴾, that is: with clear, manifest signs indicating that they are messengers from Allah.

An example of that: Allah, glory be to Him, sent Moses to Pharaoh and gave him clear signs. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We certainly gave Moses nine clear signs. So ask the Children of Israel, when he came to them...﴾ [al-Isra 101]. Among them: the wondrous staff. An ordinary staff, but in it are signs from the signs of Allah. Among its signs: when the skilled, proficient sorcerers gathered by Pharaoh's command and his support, and threw their ropes and staffs, and these ropes and staffs became as if they were snakes and serpents, frightening people, so that Moses, peace be upon him, sensed fear within himself, because it was beyond imagination: skilled sorcerers who brought all their strength and threw, filling the earth with ropes and staffs, so these ropes and staffs became as if they were snakes and serpents. ﴿When they threw, they bewitched the eyes of the people, terrified them, and produced a great magic﴾ [al-A'raf 116]. Allah revealed to him to throw the staff; he threw it, and this staff turned into a great serpent and began to swallow what they had falsified. All the ropes they had brought, this serpent swallowed. This is one of the great signs of Allah. How could this serpent swallow all this world? Where does it go? But it is—and Allah knows best—that as soon as it swallows them they become like vapour and vanish; otherwise, the belly of this serpent could not contain them. But this is a sign! Is it not so, my brothers? You now imagine this event as a report, but what do you think if you had seen it with your own eyes? The matter would have been more severe and greater. We now picture it only through report and in the mind, but if you witnessed the matter you would know it is a great sign.

The second sign of this staff: his people asked him for water, so he struck a rock, and twelve springs gushed forth from it. The water sprang from this rock that he struck with the staff, because the Children of Israel were twelve tribal leaders. Is this not a sign? Indeed it is: a deaf stone from which springs gush forth without digging and without anything else, a sign from the signs of Allah.

The third sign: when Pharaoh overtook Moses, peace be upon him, and drove them toward the sea, the companions of Moses became certain they were doomed and said: "Indeed we are overtaken." They had no escape: the sea was before them, if they crossed it they would drown, and Pharaoh and his troops were behind them and would destroy them. ﴿The companions of Moses said: Indeed we are overtaken﴾ [al-Shu'ara 61]. But look at the faith and certainty: ﴿He said: No! Indeed my Lord is with me; He will guide me﴾ [al-Shu'ara 62], that is: He will show me what holds deliverance. So Allah revealed to him: ﴿Strike the sea with your staff﴾ [al-Shu'ara 63], and he struck the sea once with the staff, and it split into twelve paths according to the number of the tribal leaders of the Children of Israel. ﴿Each portion was like a great mountain﴾ [al-Shu'ara 63], that is, like a great mountain. The land immediately dried: ﴿So strike for them a dry path through the sea﴾ [Ta-Ha 77], and the water was on their right and on their left like mountains. Look also at their faith: how they entered these paths with the water on their right and left, because of faith, for they knew they would be saved without doubt. These are among the signs of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, was given by Allah clear signs: he healed the blind from birth and the leper by Allah's permission, and these two ailments have no remedy known to physicians to this day, except that the blind-from-birth may sometimes be treated. He raised the dead by Allah's permission; he would say to a bier in front of people: "Rise," and it would rise by Allah's permission. He would bring the dead out of their graves: he would stand at a grave and command its occupant to come out, and he would come out alive. Who can do this except Allah the Mighty and Majestic? Allah made this a sign for that prophet.

He would create from clay the likeness of a bird and then breathe into it, and it would fly! Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Then it becomes a bird by Allah's permission﴾ [Al 'Imran 49]. In a second reading: ﴿Then it becomes a flying bird﴾. If you combine the two readings the meaning becomes: a bird by Allah's permission that flies, because not every bird flies; the ostrich has wings but does not fly. Rather, it becomes a bird that flies, observed in the air. And he created it from clay! Who can do this? Resurrection after death and bringing into existence from non-existence: no one can do this except Allah. Allah made it a sign for Jesus.

If someone asks: Why did Allah single out Moses with the staff, and Jesus with the raising of the dead and the creation of birds?

The people of knowledge said: Allah the Mighty is Wise; He gives each prophet the signs that suit the time and the state of the people, so as to overwhelm them. They say: magic had reached a high level in the time of Moses, so Allah showed them a sign against which their sorcery was powerless. For this reason, in the story of Moses, the sorcerers, who knew magic, could not restrain themselves except to believe: ﴿And the sorcerers were thrown down prostrate﴾ [al-A'raf 120]. They were thrown down prostrate; they did not prostrate by choice, as if without will; they were stunned and so prostrated, and they declared publicly: ﴿We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Moses and Aaron﴾ [al-A'raf 121-122].

In the time of Jesus, medicine advanced greatly, so Allah gave him a sign that physicians could not match.

As for Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him and his family, he was sent in a time of great eloquence which had reached its peak among the Arabs, and the Arabic tongue is the most eloquent of tongues and the most indicative of what is in the mind. So Allah sent him with the Noble Qur'an, which made the Arabs unable to produce its like, and neither jinn nor humans will ever produce its like. Allah the Mighty said: ﴿Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, even if some of them were to support others﴾ [al-Isra 88]. Even if some of them helped others, they would not produce its like. Allah the Mighty has spoken truly. The Qur'an is the speech of Allah; just as Allah has nothing like Him, His speech has nothing like it. ﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear evidences﴾ [al-Hadid 25].

It is related from the Prophet ﷺ: "Allah, the Exalted, never sent a prophet without giving him signs by which people would believe, similar to them, until proof is established." He said: "What I was given is a revelation which Allah revealed to me, so I hope to be the one with the most followers among them."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4981) and Muslim (152 / 239) from Abu Hurayrah.]] What he hoped for has come to pass, praise be to Allah. The one with the most followers among the prophets is Muhammad ﷺ, because his greatest sign is the Mighty Qur'an. The Mighty Qur'an remains; all people read it and derive from it signs that increase them in faith, and by it they know the truthfulness of the Prophet ﷺ.

If someone asks: What is the need for prophets to be given signs?

We say: The need is established, indeed a necessity, indeed also a matter of reason; for it is not reasonable that a person comes and says, "I am a messenger," and then is followed. There must be a clear proof showing that he is a messenger.

If a person had come, in a nation other than the nation of Muhammad, peace be upon him, and said he was a messenger without bringing a sign, the people would be excused for not following him; otherwise every person would claim to be a messenger. After the Prophet ﷺ, prophethood has ended, because he was the Seal of the Prophets. Therefore, the prophets must have signs that prove their truthfulness and the soundness of what they brought of the law.

﴿And We sent down with them the Book and the balance﴾ [al-Hadid 25]. The Book: the revelation which Allah revealed to them. Every messenger had a book with him, unlike the prophet, for a prophet may not have a book with him, but a messenger must have a book with him, because a messenger must give the people he calls what they can see with their eyes.

His saying: ﴿the Book﴾: is it singular or is the genus meant?

The genus is meant, that is, the books; for He said: ﴿Our messengers with clear evidences and sent down with them the Book﴾; it is not one book, but every messenger had a book.

His saying: ﴿and the balance﴾, that is: justice, by which things are weighed and their worth and condition are known. This clearly indicates that sound analogy (qiyas) is among what the messengers were sent with, because analogy is equating a branch with a root in a ruling for a common cause. Allah the Mighty said: ﴿And We sent down with them the Book and the balance﴾ [al-Hadid 25], that is: justice and comparison among matters.

﴿That people may uphold justice﴾ [al-Hadid 25], that is: that people may uphold justice in religion and in worldly life, by justice toward Allah and toward the servants. What is justice toward Allah?

Justice toward Allah is what the Prophet ﷺ mentioned to Mu'adh ibn Jabal when he said to him: "Do you know, O Mu'adh, what is the right of Allah over the servants, and what is the right of the servants over Allah?" He said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "The right of Allah over the servants is that they worship Him and do not associate anything with Him, and the right of the servants over Allah is that He does not punish one who does not associate anything with Him."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2856) and Muslim (30 / 48) from Mu'adh ibn Jabal.]]

His saying, meaning that He does not punish one who worships Him and does not associate anything with Him, is the right of the created. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever loves to be drawn away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise, let his death come while he believes in Allah and the Last Day, and let him treat people with what he loves to be treated with."[[Related by Muslim (1844 / 46) from Abdullah ibn Amr.]] This is the evidence: that you deal with people by what you love them to deal with you. If we dealt with people by this, justice would be established and no one would dare to wrong another. And if we felt for people what we feel for ourselves, mercy and humility would settle in our hearts, because every person loves to be treated by people with mercy and humility; so treat people with mercy and humility too.

Then Allah, blessed and exalted, mentioned what victory is achieved by from another direction, because victory comes through revelation and comes through might, and this is what He mentioned in His saying: ﴿And We sent down iron, wherein is great military might﴾, and so on to the end.

﴿And We sent down iron﴾, that is: We created it for them from the minerals. Some scholars inferred from His saying "We sent down iron" that a mineral found at the peaks of mountains is stronger and more beneficial than one found at the bottom, because descent is only from above. Allah knows best. This relates to the science of geology. But "sent down" means: We placed iron for them, and it is a well-known mineral, among the strongest of minerals.

﴿Wherein is great military might and benefits for people﴾: great might in war; swords, daggers and all instruments of war are made from it. He mentioned it after the mention of the Books because religion is not established except by this: by call and by fighting. When the disbelievers refuse that the religion of Allah be supreme, then they are fought, and with what? With iron. ﴿Wherein is great military might﴾, that is: in war.

﴿And benefits for people﴾: the word "benefits" is in the plural because its kinds cannot be counted, let alone its types and individual items. Who can count for me the benefits obtained from iron? We give you a week's time; you cannot count them, you cannot. For this reason it came in the plural form of the highest plural pattern: ﴿and benefits for people﴾, religious and worldly, individual and social.

﴿And that Allah may make evident who supports Him and His messengers unseen﴾ is coordinated with ﴿that people may uphold justice﴾.

His saying: ﴿And that Allah may make evident who supports Him﴾: what is meant is knowledge of manifestation upon which reward or punishment is based. As for knowledge that it will occur, this precedes the sending of messengers and the sending down of books, because Allah has always been and always will be Knowing of everything. So do not let the matter confuse you; do not say that Allah knows only after this. We say: Yes.

Knowledge is of two kinds: knowledge of a thing before its existence, and knowledge of a thing after its existence. Which knowledge is the one upon which reward and punishment are based? The second or the first? The second, because prior knowledge does not entail reward or punishment, until people are tested.

So: "that Allah may know" means knowledge of manifestation, that is, that it became manifest and actually occurred. This is one; and knowledge upon which reward and punishment are based. As for knowledge that it will occur, this is known to Allah from eternity.

﴿Who supports Him﴾: that is, supports His religion, and the meaning is not that one supports Allah Himself; no, because Allah is free of need from the worlds. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿That, and had Allah willed, He would have taken vengeance upon them, but that He may test some of you by means of others. And those who are killed in the way of Allah—He will never waste their deeds﴾ [Muhammad 4]. So ﴿supports Him﴾: how do you interpret it? "Supports His religion." If someone said to you: How does He support His religion when Allah says: ﴿Who supports Him﴾? This is an interpretation contrary to the wording, and you reject those who interpret the Qur'an in a way that contradicts its apparent wording. So what is the answer?

The answer: We do not reject people who interpret the Qur'an contrary to its apparent wording when that is supported by evidence. If that is supported by evidence, we do not reject it. For this reason, if someone says regarding His saying: ﴿So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan﴾ [al-Nahl 98], that the meaning is: "when you intend to recite the Qur'an," he has interpreted it contrary to its apparent sense. Do we say this interpretation is correct or incorrect? Correct, because a person seeks refuge in Allah when he intends to recite, not when he has finished reciting, by the practice of the Prophet ﷺ, and because this is what indicates that a person should seek refuge in Allah before reciting, so that Satan stays far from him.

In any case, if someone says to you: How do you interpret His saying: ﴿Who supports Him﴾, that is, who supports His religion, while you reject those who interpret the Qur'an contrary to its apparent sense?

The answer: We do not reject one who interprets the Qur'an contrary to its apparent sense if there is a sound evidence for it. The evidence that the meaning is "supports His religion" is His saying: ﴿Indeed Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might﴾, who needs no one; He is Powerful and Exalted, Victorious with a strength that is never touched by weakness.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 57, verse 25 (part 2 of 2):

Regarding the words of the Most High: ﴿Who supports Him and His messengers﴾. The support of the messengers: is what is meant that one supports the Messenger himself, or that one supports the sharia (religious law) he brought? Both are meant. If the Messenger is alive, what is meant is supporting the Messenger himself and his sharia; after his death, one supports his sharia. In this is evidence that supporting the sharia is supporting the one who brought it. Nor does it pose a problem for this that Allah, glorified and exalted, may cause the Messenger to die before he sees the wide victory granted to him, because we say: supporting his sharia is supporting him.

And His words: ﴿unseen﴾, meaning that they support Allah, mighty and majestic, and support His messengers while they have not seen Allah, because Allah, exalted, is supported and not seen. He is not seen in this world. For this reason some of the early scholars (salaf) said: "They support Him and do not see Him," as an explanation of His words ﴿unseen﴾: they support Him and do not see Him, and what is meant is that they do not see Him in this world. As for the Hereafter, the sight of Allah, exalted, is true and established in the Qur'an, the Sunnah and the consensus (ijma') of the Companions.

So: ﴿unseen﴾ means they support Allah while He is unseen. It may also be that the meaning of ﴿unseen﴾ is: in their absence from people, and in this is evidence of their sincerity, and that they are not among those who worship Allah only when among people, but rather they worship Allah, exalted, both in the unseen and in the witnessed.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Strong, Mighty﴾. This sentence is a resumptive clause to show that the support of Allah, mighty and majestic, is not out of weakness or compulsion, but rather He is Strong and Mighty, who does not need anyone to support Him in Himself, but rather the support is for His religion.

We ask Allah to make us and you among the supporters of His religion.

This verse is emphasized with three emphatic particles: first, the omitted oath; second, the lam; and third, qad.

﴿And We had already sent Noah and Abraham, and placed in their offspring prophethood and the Scripture.﴾ [al-Hadid: 26]

Noah was the first of the messengers, peace be upon them, and he is one of the five Ulul-Azm (the resolute messengers). Abraham is the father of the prophets after him, and the prophets trace back to him, meaning to his religion (millah). For this reason, Muslims, Jews, and Christians dispute about him. The Jews say he was a Jew, the Christians say he was a Christian, and the Muslims say he was a hanif (one who turns away from falsehood to pure monotheism) and a Muslim. This last view is the truth.

It is strange that Christians and Jews say he was a Christian or a Jew, when Christianity and Judaism did not exist until after him. But they lack understanding.

﴿And We placed in their offspring﴾ meaning the offspring of Noah and Abraham, ﴿prophethood and the Scripture﴾, meaning the messengers, peace be upon them. This indicates that Adam was not a messenger, and that Idris was not before Noah, as some historians have mentioned. That is an error that contradicts the Noble Qur'an. There was no messenger before Noah. Adam was a prophet who was addressed directly by Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with whatever He willed of His revelation. Then his children followed his way after him. When people spread and multiplied, disagreement arose among them, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Mankind were one community; then Allah sent the prophets as bringers of good tidings and warners, and sent down with them the Scripture in truth, to judge between the people concerning that over which they differed﴾ [al-Baqarah: 213]. As for His saying ﴿and the Scripture﴾, it refers to the category (jins), because every messenger had a scripture, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿We had certainly sent Our messengers with clear evidences, and sent down with them the Scripture and the Balance that people may maintain justice﴾.

﴿So among them is one who is guided, but many of them are defiant﴾ [al-Hadid: 26]. The word "minhum" means some of them are guided. The letter yā' in the word "muhtadin" has been dropped, as is the rule in the Arabic language. Its original form is "muhtadiyun" (مهتدي) with the yā', but it was dropped for ease of pronunciation.

﴿And many of them are defiant﴾ meaning they are not guided. This is the reality: most of the children of Adam are astray, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And if you obey most of those on earth, they will lead you astray from the way of Allah﴾ [al-An'am: 116].

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 57, verse 27:**

﴿Then We sent, following in their footsteps, Our messengers, and We sent after them Jesus, son of Mary, and gave him the Injil (Gospel)﴾ [al-Hadid: 27]

﴿qaffayna﴾ means "We caused to follow," derived from *al-qafa* (the back of the neck), because whoever walks behind your back is following you.

﴿ʿala athariham﴾ means: in the footsteps of Noah, Abraham, and the other messengers who came before.

﴿bi-rusulina﴾ means: those who followed them.

﴿wa-qaffayna bi-ʿIsa ibni Maryam wa-ataynahu al-Injil﴾ Allah specified him because there is no messenger or prophet between him and Muhammad (ﷺ). Between them there is neither a messenger nor a prophet. As for what is claimed about Khalid ibn Maʿdan and others that they had prophethood, it is all falsehood.

﴿wa-ataynahu al-Injil﴾ is the Book that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Jesus. It is considered a complement to the Torah, because the Torah was the mother of the Books among the Children of Israel.

﴿wa-jaʿalna fi qulubi alladhina ittabaʿuhu raʾfatan wa-rahmatan wa-rahbaniyyatan ibtadaʿuha﴾ [al-Hadid: 27]

Allah placed three things in the hearts of the Christians who followed Jesus: compassion (*raʾfa*), mercy (*rahma*), and monasticism (*rahbaniyya*). While they followed the law of Jesus, they were among the gentlest of people in heart and the most merciful toward creation. But after they disbelieved in Muhammad, they became among the harshest of people, as you know from what happened between the Muslims and the Christians in the Crusades and elsewhere.

﴿raʾfatan wa-rahmatan﴾: *raʾfa* is gentler and more intense than *rahma*. It is a type of mercy, but finer and more tender.

﴿wa-rahbaniyya﴾ is withdrawal from the world for the sake of worship.

﴿ibtadaʿuha﴾ means: they invented it on their own, as some sects of the Muslims did. They invented a monasticism for which Allah sent down no authority. Yet they had gentleness and mercy.

﴿ma katabnaha ʿalayhim illa ibtighaʾa ridwani Allah﴾ means that We did not prescribe it for them, but they sought the good pleasure of Allah. For this reason we say that ﴿illa ibtighaʾa ridwani Allah﴾ is an *istithna' munqati'* (disconnected exception). Nevertheless, although they invented it and chose it for themselves, they did not observe it as it should be observed, meaning they did not carry out its obligatory duties, nor did they perform this monasticism that they had invented in the proper way. Rather, they manipulated it as they pleased.

﴿fa-atayna alladhina amanu minhum ajrahum﴾ means: their reward.

﴿wa-kathirun minhum fasiqun﴾ Many of these Christians are wicked, meaning they have departed from the obedience of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

In this there is evidence that when a person innovates an innovation (*bidʿa*), he is not granted success in upholding it. He is misguided in its origin and misguided in its details, even if he strives and even if he is humble.

You will find some people who have invented remembrances, prayers, supplications, or the like. You find them humble, their hearts weeping and submissive, but it does not benefit them, because they are upon misguidance.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger; He will give you a double portion of His mercy﴾ [al-Hadid 28]. ﴿O you who have believed﴾ refers to this Ummah.

So His saying ﴿fear Allah and believe in His Messenger﴾ means: remain steadfast upon faith, not renew faith, because faith has already been attained, as He said ﴿O you who have believed﴾. The meaning, then, is: O you who have believed with your hearts, fear Allah with your limbs, and ﴿believe in His Messenger﴾, that is, realize the faith and remain steadfast upon it. Not everyone who believes is a true believer. This is what the scholars mean when they say: "This is a negation of the perfection of faith," like His saying (ﷺ): "None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (13) and Muslim (45/71), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik]. The intent is not the negation of faith in its absolute sense, but the negation of complete, perfect faith.

Some exegetes have claimed that this verse is addressed to the People of the Book, because He says ﴿and believe in His Messenger﴾. But this view is very weak, and it is impossible for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to address the People of the Book with the description of faith while they are disbelievers. That is, it is not possible that His saying ﴿O you who have believed﴾ means "O Jews and Christians," because when the Qur'an was revealed, if they remained upon their Judaism and Christianity, they were not believers.

﴿Believe, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger﴾. Here, "His Messenger" means Muhammad (ﷺ), and belief in the Messenger (ﷺ) includes belief in all the messengers, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and so do the believers. Each one believes in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers. We make no distinction between any of His messengers﴾ [al-Baqarah 285]. That is, in belief in them; not in following them. In following, we distinguish between the messengers: which of them do we follow? Muhammad (ﷺ). But in belief, all of them are equal; we believe that they are truly the messengers of Allah.

﴿He will give you a double portion of His mercy﴾ [al-Hadid 28], that is, two shares of Allah's mercy. For this reason, the Prophet (ﷺ) likened this Ummah, in comparison to those before it, to a man who hired workers: some from the beginning of the day until midday, some from midday until the afternoon prayer, and some from the afternoon prayer until sunset. He gave each of the first group a dinar, and each of the second group a dinar, and each of the third group two dinars. The first group objected: "Why do you give these two dinars when they have done less work than us?" He answered them: "Have I wronged you in your wage at all?" They said: "No." He said: "That is My bounty, which I give to whom I will" [al-Bukhari (2268), from the hadith of Ibn Umar]. Praise be to Allah. So this Ummah has the reward of the previous nations twice over.

﴿And He will make for you a light by which you walk﴾: that is, if you believe and realize the faith together with piety, He will reward you with a double reward. ﴿And He will make for you a light by which you walk﴾, that is, knowledge by which you travel toward Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, with insight.

In this is evidence that piety is among the causes of acquiring knowledge. Many are those who seek knowledge, seeking memorization, that is, they seek to acquire it, seeking understanding. We say: its attainment is easy, by fearing Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and realizing the faith, which necessitates knowledge. Act upon what you know, and what you did not know will be granted to you. Fear of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is undoubtedly among the causes of increased knowledge. For this reason He said: ﴿And He will make for you a light by which you walk﴾, that is, you walk by it, by means of it, a sound walk that brings you to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

﴿And He will forgive you﴾, that is, He will cover it over for you and pardon you, so there is neither punishment nor disgrace. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, that is, Possessor of forgiveness and mercy, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Indeed your Lord is full of forgiveness for mankind despite their wrongdoing﴾ [al-Ra'd 6], and He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And your Lord is the Forgiving, Possessor of mercy﴾ [al-Kahf 58]. So "al-Ghafur" means Possessor of forgiveness, and "al-Rahim" means Possessor of mercy. This is because a person needs forgiveness for sins he has committed, and mercy that keeps him steady, by which he avoids acts of disobedience and is guided to repentance if he disobeys.

Then He says: ﴿So that the People of the Scripture may know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of Allah﴾ [al-Hadid 29]. That is: He made this reward for you so that the People of the Scripture would know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of Allah, and that they cannot envy you for what Allah has given you of His bounty, despite their intense effort to envy the Prophet (ﷺ), as the Exalted said: ﴿Many of the People of the Scripture wish they could turn you back to disbelief after your belief, out of envy from themselves﴾ [al-Baqarah 109].

Here, the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿So that the People of the Scripture may know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of Allah﴾, neither to give nor to withhold. ﴿And that bounty is in the hand of Allah﴾ [al-Hadid 29], the Mighty and Majestic, who manages everything He wills according to what His wisdom requires. ﴿And Allah is the Possessor of great bounty﴾ [al-Hadid 29]; that is, the Possessor of great bounty. How great is the bounty of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, upon His servants! The Exalted said: ﴿And whatever blessing you have is from Allah; then when adversity touches you, to Him you cry for help﴾ [al-Nahl 53].

We ask Allah, the Exalted, to grant us and you of His bounty, and to bestow upon us of His mercy, for He is the Bestower. May the blessings and peace of Allah be upon our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), and upon his family and all his companions.
